These are rolmu, rolso, roldelbzolso, rolsolhso, roldewdujucese, rolduwsozezo, roldezoceju and rolnuzezo (e.g., roldewdujucese cero > juroldewdujucese jucero).

Similarly, most nouns beginning with rowl- change to ziql- in the plural. Examples of this pattern include rowlmu, rowlzoriso, rowlcize, rowlzowcoqriju, rowldelzodu, and rowlzoduwde (e.g., rowlzoduwde bq > ziqlzoduwde jucek 'stained-glass windows'). However, some rowl- nouns do not follow this pattern and form their plural with ju-, notably rowlzo, rowlzowdudul, rowlkblhso, rowlduzek, rowlbzocedeqrinu and rowlduzorico (e.g., rowlzo cero > jurowlzo jucero 'the rails').

* Case
Nouns in Hsobcezose are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

----------
ADJECTIVES
----------

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Hsobcezose adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like qlcemu and qlcedeqrib, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in l, ce, w, ri, q, me, ze, è and some occurrences of h, e.g. bwkzolç qlcemu bq (a beautiful garden), cecicirih rocemu bq (a handsome man), cecicicese cerorocemu cebq (a beautiful woman), judublsebce ziqlcemu jucero (the beautiful children), jubrijuwlci jucerorocemu jucero (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix ce- to the masculine form, e.g., kblzonu > cekblzonu, dubcero > cedubcero, bljuzoceco > cebljuzoceco. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with roce-, row-, bri-, bce-, juri- or jul- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix ce- (e.g., roceqzoso > ceroroceqzoso, rowdubcenu > cerorowdubcenu, brimu > cebbrimu, bcewsobl > cebbcewsobl, jurizonu > cejujurizonu, and julmu > cejujulmu).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with so- change to cehso- (e.g., soblromu > cehsoblromu); those beginning with zoqce- or ziqce- change to cejuqce- (e.g., zoqceduducecirizoco > cejuqceduducecirizoco, ziqcewzoqse > cejuqcewzoqse), with the exception of the irregular ziqcewde (old) whose feminine form is cerorowcewde; nu- changes to ceqnu- (e.g., nubriro > ceqnubriro); sew- changes to cedew- (e.g., sewdusol > cedewdusol); sece- changes to cedeè- (e.g., secezomu > cedeèzomu); zoce- changes to cezoè- (e.g., zocenublzoduze > cezoènublzoduze); duce- changes to ceduè- (e.g., ducewqybw > ceduèwqybw); and adjectives beginning with qri- have a special form rori- (becoming cerorori- in feminine) that appears after l, ce, w, ri, q, me, ze, è and some occurrences of h, (e.g., qrise/rorise > cerororise, qrici/rorici > cerororici).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with ce-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. cehsowzo cecicirih bq 'a rich man' > cehsowzo cecicicese cebq 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix ju- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., wroriç > juwroriç, cewroriç > jucewroriç). If the basic form beginning with ju-, zi-, or f-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., julmu > julmu, ziqcezozebzenu > ziqcezozebzenu, ziqrik > ziqrik), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Hsobcezose adjectives beginning with qlce- take the prefix zi- in the masculine plural (e.g., qlcedeqrib > ziqlcedeqrib). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with rol-, which normally change to ziql- in the masculine plural (e.g., rolbzocedewh > ziqlbzocedewh, rolzodubceso > ziqlzodubceso), with only two exceptions: roldulse > juroldulse and roldelb > juroldelb which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: cerolzodubceso > jucerolzodubceso.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed before the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in cenuqrizo bwde cero (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically follow their nouns. These are qlcemu (beautiful), brimu (good), secezomu (brief), kblzonu (big/tall), jurizonu (fat/large), ziqlse (false), duqlh (high), nubriro (long), secezomu (brief), cebqceç (young), wroriç (pretty), juwldeqlci (bad), zoqcerorowceci (better), qlcedeqrib (new), duwduceco (small), ziqcewde (old); e.g., cecicicese cerorocemu cebq ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Hsobcezose, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
hsobcezose personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | ceç
         | 2nd (informal)   | qdu
         | 2nd (formal)     | juqride
         | 3rd (masculine)  | row
         | 3rd (feminine)   | ceroroce
         | 3rd (neutral)    | bri
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | juqrib
         | 2nd              | juqride
         | 3rd (masculine)  | jurow
         | 3rd (feminine)   | juceroroce
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun ceç occurs after l, ce, w, ri, q, me, ze, è, ê and some occurrences of h, it becomes 'ç.

*Relative pronouns

hsobcezose, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Hsobcezose, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, wqy is ordinarily used: ceduducerosomesowmu lci zeroride l wqy cecicirih'ro ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that wqy in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: jucezeroride zeduze dubri wqy juceduducerosomesowmu jucero ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, ceqy (or 'qy after l, ce, w, ri, q, me, ze, è, ê and some occurrences of h) is ordinarily used: cezeroride l row'qy ceduducerosomesowmu lro ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like wqy, ceqy does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Hsobcezose are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Hsobcezose is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) zowridel ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of cezoduê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is cezoduê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is zowridel. Forms of cezoduê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Hsobcezose, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

hsobcezose verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -jujuw- between the stem and the ending.

    In dubcewlrozolco, the stem -rozolco indicates that the verb is zocerozolco (to speak) and the prefix dubcewl- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In jubrijujuwbwse, the stem -bwse indicates that the verb is zowbwse (to finish), the prefix -jujuw- precedes it, and the inflection jubri- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Hsobcezose they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    zocerozolco: juwlzocerozolco ceç, julrozolco qdu, dubcejujulrozolco jurow'qy, jubriwrozolco juqrib ceqy, fcerozolco...
    zowbwse: juwlzowbwse ceç, juceduîbwse juqride, dubcejujuwbwse jurow'qy, juwbwse, jubriwjujuwbwse juqrib ceqy...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    zowriroqride: ziqcede ceç, ziqcede qdu, duqcede row, jubriroqride juqrib, fceroqride juqride, dubceroqcede jurow.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly zowridel, cezoduê, zocerorol and cezowlse), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with zoce- (with the exception of zocerorol, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    zoceciwl, zocemelrolmu, zocedublhso, zocemeridebce, zocecizocese, zocenublci, zocejujulco, zocemelco, zocebcecirizoco, zocekzolnucezo, etc.

        For example, for the verb zocerozolco, the stem is -rozolco and the infinitive prefix is zoce-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with zow- whose present participle begins with dubljujuw-:

    zowbzemu, zowdulcociriso, zowcozoceqnuzek, zowzoqcerose, zowkblzonu, zoïlh, zowdujucedebw, zowrorico, zownuqrizo, zownuqzo, zowrolju, etc.

        For example, for the verb zowbwse, the stem is -bwse and the infinitive prefix is zow-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries cezoduê and zowridel, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. cekzolnucezo ceç means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with zoce- (all verbs of the first group): ce-, juce-, ce-, jubri-, fce-, dubce-.
    Verbs beginning with zow- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): juw-, juw-, duw-, jubrijujuw-, fcejujuw-, dubcejujuw-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with cezo- (part of the third group): ju-, ju-, - , jubri-, fce-, dubce-.
    
    Example:

-------------------------------

2nd person     | jucekzolnucezo qdu        | fcekzolnucezo juqride
3rd person     | cekzolnucezo bri/ceroroce/row | dubcekzolnucezo juceroroce/jurow

**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "juwlkzolnucezo ceç" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.
    For the first group, the stem is the infinitive minus the zoce- prefix, e.g., zocekzolnucezo -> -kzolnucezo.
    For the second group, the stem is the infinitive minus the zow- prefix plus the jujuw- prefix, e.g., zowjuwrihso -> -jujuwjuwrihso. 
    And for the third group, the stem is derived from the first person plural of the present indicative.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: juwl-, juwl-, duwl-, jubriw-, fcew-, dubcewl-.

The future prefixes correspond to the present indicative of the verb zowridel. They are always regular: wl-, jul-, l-, jubri-, fce-, dubri-.

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding ce- and ju- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "duwsebriso duwqzose bq", "ceduwsebriso cezowrico cebq", "juduwsebriso juduwqzose jucek", and "juceduwsebriso jucezowrico jucek."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with ze- for the 1st group verbs, and with w- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : q- (cezokbcedubce qkbcedubce, cezowrimu qmu, cezowro qro, etc. and zowridelju qju, zowride qde, zowrideqrico qco), juw- (cezoduduceci juwci, cezokbcezoco juwzoco, etc.), juq- (cezoqrosobw juqrosobw and cezoqrosocezo juqrosocezo and only these verbs), duw- (cezowkqlci duwkqlci, cezowk duwk, etc.), du- (verbs in cezokbw- : cezokbwceco dubwceco), duzoce- (zowzodeqri duzocedeqri, zowzodeqriso duzocedeqriso, zowzoseseri duzoceseseri and zowzoseseqriju duzoceseseqriju), or qce (zowridel qce). 

*Compound Tenses

hsobcezose compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either zowridel or cezoduê) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Hsobcezose, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Hsobcezose. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either zowridel or cezoduê in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "zenublci wl'ç" (I ate) or "zedewzozol dujuce row" (He arrived). zowridel is used with most verbs, while cezoduê is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, zowridel should be used by default.

*Past participle agreement

The past participle is used in three ways in Hsobcezose: as an adjective, in the passive construction, and in the compound tense constructions. When it is used as an adjective, it follows all the regular adjective agreement rules. In passive constructions, it always agrees with the passive subject.

In compound tense forms (such as the compound past), more complicated agreement rules apply, reflecting the subtle priority rules between the attribute meaning (which implies an agreement) and the compound tense construction (which by itself does not imply any agreement).

A. The auxiliary verb is zowridel.

    If there is no direct object (the verb is intransitive) or the direct object appears before the past participle, then the past participle does not agree (i.e., it takes the default masculine singular form).
        (intransitive) wcizorik dubri juceroroce. ("They (fem.) slept.")
        (direct object before verb) jucebwcerolmu ziqcek qde l cezowlroso. ("cezowlroso saw two whales.")
    If there is a direct object and it appears after the past participle, then the participle must agree with it. Three cases:
        (pronoun after the auxiliary) jucebwcerolmu ziqcek duwldel me row. juceqde l jucero cezowlroso. ("There were two whales. cezowlroso saw them.")
        (clause-final wh-question element)  juceqde ceroroce-du-l cezowlroso jucebwcerolmu juceroroceqy? ("Which whales did cezowlroso see?")
        (relative clause linked by ceqy) juceqde l cezowlroso ceqy jucebwcerolmu ziqcek jucero ("the two whales that cezowlroso saw")
    The above rule is one of the most difficult in Hsobcezose.

B. The auxiliary is cezoduê, and the verb is not reflexive. The past participle agrees with the subject:

        jucezedewzozol dubriju juceroroce. ("They (fem.) arrived.")

C. The auxiliary is cezoduê and the verb is reflexive. The agreement rules are in fact the same as those for structures with zowridel in A, keeping in mind that the reflexive pronoun corresponds to either the direct object or the indirect object of the verb.

* Case
Nouns in Hcixgçuî are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

----------
ADJECTIVES
----------

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Hcixgçuî adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like timugpè and timugmètiêx, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in mu, g, v, ê, ti, lœ, æ, e and some occurrences of h, e.g. xvtéçumud timugpè xti (a beautiful garden), gñuñuêh kgpè xti (a handsome man), gñuñugî gkkgpè gxti (a beautiful woman), lèûxmuîxg cètimugpè lègk (the beautiful children), lèxêlèvmuñu lègkkgpè lègk (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix g- to the masculine form, e.g., téxmuçujœ > gtéxmuçujœ, ûxgk > gûxgk, xmulèçugcu > gxmulèçugcu. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with kg-, kv-, xê-, xg-, lèê- or lèmu- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix g- (e.g., kgtiçuci > gkkgtiçuci, kvûxgjœ > gkkvûxgjœ, xêpè > gxxêpè, xgvcixmu > gxxgvcixmu, lèêçujœ > glèlèêçujœ, and lèmupè > glèlèmupè).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with ci- change to ghci- (e.g., cixmukpè > ghcixmukpè); those beginning with çutig- or cètig- change to glètig- (e.g., çutigûûgñuêçucu > glètigûûgñuêçucu, cètigvçutiî > glètigvçutiî), with the exception of the irregular cètigvmè (old) whose feminine form is gkkvgvmè; jœ- changes to gtijœ- (e.g., jœxêk > gtijœxêk); îv- changes to gmèv- (e.g., îvûcimu > gmèvûcimu); îg- changes to gmèe- (e.g., îgçupè > gmèeçupè); çug- changes to gçue- (e.g., çugjœxmuçuûæ > gçuejœxmuçuûæ); ûg- changes to gûe- (e.g., ûgvticéxv > gûevticéxv); and adjectives beginning with tiê- have a special form kê- (becoming gkkê- in feminine) that appears after mu, g, v, ê, ti, lœ, æ, e and some occurrences of h, (e.g., tiêî/kêî > gkkêî, tiêñu/kêñu > gkkêñu).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with g-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. ghcivçu gñuñuêh xti 'a rich man' > ghcivçu gñuñugî gxti 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix lè- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., vkêd > lèvkêd, gvkêd > lègvkêd). If the basic form beginning with lè-, cè-, or cœ-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., lèmupè > lèmupè, cètigçuæxæjœ > cètigçuæxæjœ, cètiêté > cètiêté), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Hcixgçuî adjectives beginning with timug- take the prefix cè- in the masculine plural (e.g., timugmètiêx > cètimugmètiêx). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with kmu-, which normally change to cètimu- in the masculine plural (e.g., kmuxçugmèvh > cètimuxçugmèvh, kmuçuûxgci > cètimuçuûxgci), with only two exceptions: kmuûmuî > lèkmuûmuî and kmumèmux > lèkmumèmux which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: gkmuçuûxgci > lègkmuçuûxgci.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed before the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in gjœtiêçu xvmè gk (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically follow their nouns. These are timugpè (beautiful), xêpè (good), îgçupè (brief), téxmuçujœ (big/tall), lèêçujœ (fat/large), cètimuî (false), ûtimuh (high), jœxêk (long), îgçupè (brief), gxtigd (young), vkêd (pretty), lèvmumètimuñu (bad), çutigkkvgñu (better), timugmètiêx (new), ûvûgcu (small), cètigvmè (old); e.g., gñuñugî gkkgpè gxti ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Hcixgçuî, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
hcixgçuî personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | gd
         | 2nd (informal)   | tiû
         | 2nd (formal)     | lètiêmè
         | 3rd (masculine)  | kv
         | 3rd (feminine)   | gkkg
         | 3rd (neutral)    | xê
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | lètiêx
         | 2nd              | lètiêmè
         | 3rd (masculine)  | lèkv
         | 3rd (feminine)   | lègkkg
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun gd occurs after mu, g, v, ê, ti, lœ, æ, e, z and some occurrences of h, it becomes 'd.

*Relative pronouns

hcixgçuî, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Hcixgçuî, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, vticé is ordinarily used: gûûgkcilœcivpè muñu ækêmè mu vticé gñuñuêh'k ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that vticé in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: lègækêmè æûæ ûxê vticé lègûûgkcilœcivpè lègk ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, gticé (or 'ticé after mu, g, v, ê, ti, lœ, æ, e, z and some occurrences of h) is ordinarily used: gækêmè mu kv'ticé gûûgkcilœcivpè muk ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like vticé, gticé does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Hcixgçuî are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Hcixgçuî is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) çuvêmèmu ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of gçuûz ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is gçuûz, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is çuvêmèmu. Forms of gçuûz are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Hcixgçuî, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

hcixgçuî verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -lèlèv- between the stem and the ending.

    In ûxgvmukçumucu, the stem -kçumucu indicates that the verb is çugkçumucu (to speak) and the prefix ûxgvmu- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In lèxêlèlèvxvî, the stem -xvî indicates that the verb is çuvxvî (to finish), the prefix -lèlèv- precedes it, and the inflection lèxê- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Hcixgçuî they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    çugkçumucu: lèvmuçugkçumucu gd, lèmukçumucu tiû, ûxglèlèmukçumucu lèkv'ticé, lèxêvkçumucu lètiêx gticé, cœgkçumucu...
    çuvxvî: lèvmuçuvxvî gd, lègûñixvî lètiêmè, ûxglèlèvxvî lèkv'ticé, lèvxvî, lèxêvlèlèvxvî lètiêx gticé...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    çuvêktiêmè: cètigmè gd, cètigmè tiû, ûtigmè kv, lèxêktiêmè lètiêx, cœgktiêmè lètiêmè, ûxgktigmè lèkv.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly çuvêmèmu, gçuûz, çugkkmu and gçuvmuî), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with çug- (with the exception of çugkkmu, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    çugñuvmu, çuglœmukmupè, çugûxmuhci, çuglœêmèxg, çugñuçugî, çugjœxmuñu, çuglèlèmucu, çuglœmucu, çugxgñuêçucu, çugtéçumujœgçu, etc.

        For example, for the verb çugkçumucu, the stem is -kçumucu and the infinitive prefix is çug-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with çuv- whose present participle begins with ûxmulèlèv-:

    çuvxæpè, çuvûmucuñuêci, çuvcuçugtijœæté, çuvçutigkî, çuvtéxmuçujœ, çuïmuh, çuvûlègmèxv, çuvkêcu, çuvjœtiêçu, çuvjœtiçu, çuvkmulè, etc.

        For example, for the verb çuvxvî, the stem is -xvî and the infinitive prefix is çuv-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries gçuûz and çuvêmèmu, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. gtéçumujœgçu gd means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with çug- (all verbs of the first group): g-, lèg-, g-, lèxê-, cœg-, ûxg-.
    Verbs beginning with çuv- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): lèv-, lèv-, ûv-, lèxêlèlèv-, cœglèlèv-, ûxglèlèv-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with gçu- (part of the third group): lè-, lè-, - , lèxê-, cœg-, ûxg-.
    
    Example:

**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "lèvmutéçumujœgçu gd" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.
    For the first group, the stem is the infinitive minus the çug- prefix, e.g., çugtéçumujœgçu -> -téçumujœgçu.
    For the second group, the stem is the infinitive minus the çuv- prefix plus the lèlèv- prefix, e.g., çuvlèvêhci -> -lèlèvlèvêhci. 
    And for the third group, the stem is derived from the first person plural of the present indicative.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: lèvmu-, lèvmu-, ûvmu-, lèxêv-, cœgv-, ûxgvmu-.

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding g- and lè- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "ûvîxêci ûvtiçuî xti", "gûvîxêci gçuvêcu gxti", "lèûvîxêci lèûvtiçuî lègté", and "lègûvîxêci lègçuvêcu lègté."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with æ- for the 1st group verbs, and with v- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : ti- (gçutéxgûxg titéxgûxg, gçuvêpè tipè, gçuvk tik, etc. and çuvêmèmulè tilè, çuvêmè timè, çuvêmètiêcu ticu), lèv- (gçuûûgñu lèvñu, gçutéxgçucu lèvçucu, etc.), lèti- (gçutikcixv lètikcixv and gçutikcigçu lètikcigçu and only these verbs), ûv- (gçuvtétimuñu ûvtétimuñu, gçuvté ûvté, etc.), û- (verbs in gçutéxv- : gçutéxvgcu ûxvgcu), ûçug- (çuvçumètiê ûçugmètiê, çuvçumètiêci ûçugmètiêci, çuvçuîîê ûçugîîê and çuvçuîîtiêlè ûçugîîtiêlè), or tig (çuvêmèmu tig). 

*Compound Tenses

hcixgçuî compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either çuvêmèmu or gçuûz) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Hcixgçuî, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Hcixgçuî. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either çuvêmèmu or gçuûz in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "æjœxmuñu vmu'd" (I ate) or "æmèvçuçumu ûlèg kv" (He arrived). çuvêmèmu is used with most verbs, while gçuûz is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, çuvêmèmu should be used by default.

In Àrçèbawsè, articles and determiners are required on almost every common noun, much more so than in English. They are inflected to agree in gender (masculine or feminine) and number (singular or plural) with the noun they determine, though most have only one plural form (for masculine and feminine).

* Articles
àrçèbawsè has three articles: a definite article, corresponding in many cases to English the; an indefinite article, corresponding to English a/an; and a partitive article, used roughly like some in English. 

** Definite article
 	
In Àrçèbawsè, the definite article, analogously to the English word the, is used to indicate a specific noun. However, unlike English, the Àrçèbawsè article changes based on the noun's gender (masculine or feminine) and number (singular or plural).

The definite article always comes after its noun.

For singular nouns:

- For masculine singular nouns, the article is bazi. For example, in the phrase "çiséàr bazi" (the cat), bazi shows that the noun çiséàr (cat) is both singular and masculine.
- For feminine singular nouns, the article is sézi. An example is "çèmazeysébe sézi" (the house), where sézi shows that çèmazeysébe (house) is singular and feminine.

For plural nouns, regardless of gender:

- The article is zebazi for both masculine and feminine plural nouns. (e.g., "zeçiséàr zebazi", the cats; "zeçèmazeysébe zebazi", the houses.)

In summary, bazi is used with masculine singular nouns, sézi with feminine singular nouns, and zebazi with all plural nouns. This variation in definite articles reflects the grammatical gender and number of nouns in Àrçèbawsè.

After sé, ba, y, ma, q, f, gè, ga and some occurrences of à, the singular masculine article bazi becomes 'zi.


-----
NOUNS
-----
* Gender
Every Àrçèbawsè noun has a grammatical gender, either masculine or feminine.

* Number
As in English, Àrçèbawsè nouns inflect for number, however they do so through prefixation rather than suffixation.

The plural is usually formed from the singular by adding the prefix morpheme gé- (e.g., çèmazeysébe > géçèmazeysébe 'houses'). 

Nouns beginning with qsé- and qba- take the prefix ze- instead of gé- (e.g., qséfqçi > géqséfqçi 'pipes', qbada > géqbada 'games'), except for the nouns qséseçèsézi, qséwwséze, qbaçème, and qbazix which form their plural by prefixing the morpheme ze- (e.g., qbaçème > zeqbaçème 'tires').

Seven nouns beginning with qma- form their plural with gé-. These are qmaçèbal, qmaziziysér, qmaxyà, qmadayx, qmame, qmaàr, and qmadaqmada (e.g., qmaçèbal > géqmaçèbal 'knees'). All other nouns beginning with qma-, such as qmazeyx or qmawçi, follow the regular plural pattern and take ze- (e.g., qmawçi > zeqmawçi 'holes').

Nouns that begin with ze-, gé- or p- in the singular do not change in the plural (e.g., géymawr sézi 'the cross' > géymawr zebazi 'the crosses').

Nouns that begin with zisé- typically change to géqsé- in the plural (e.g., ziséçèwqmada > géqséçèwqmada 'newspapers'). However, several nouns beginning with zisé- are exceptions to this rule and form their plural by adding ze- instead. These are ziséx, zisér, ziséhéséçèwsér, zisérséàr, ziséhéyçizebasè, ziséçiyrgèw, ziséhéwbaze and zisélgèw (e.g., ziséhéyçizebasè bazi > zeziséhéyçizebasè zebazi).

Similarly, most nouns beginning with ziysé- change to géqsé- in the plural. Examples of this pattern include ziyséx, ziyséwmar, ziysébegè, ziyséwymeqmaze, ziyséhéséwçi, and ziyséwçiyhé (e.g., ziyséwçiyhé çèq > géqséwçiyhé zebase 'stained-glass windows'). However, some ziysé- nouns do not follow this pattern and form their plural with ze-, notably ziyséw, ziyséwyçiçisé, ziyséseçèséàr, ziyséçigèse, ziyséçèwbahéqmal and ziyséçiwmame (e.g., ziyséw bazi > zeziyséw zebazi 'the rails').

* Case
Nouns in Àrçèbawsè are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

----------
ADJECTIVES
----------

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Àrçèbawsè adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like qsébax and qsébahéqmaçè, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in sé, ba, y, ma, q, f, gè, ga and some occurrences of à, e.g. çèysewséda qsébax çèq (a beautiful garden), babebemaà zibax çèq (a handsome man), babebebasè bazizibax baçèq (a beautiful woman), zeçiçèsésèçèba géqsébax zebazi (the beautiful children), zeçèmazeysébe zebazizibax zebazi (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix ba- to the masculine form, e.g., seçèséwl > baseçèséwl, çiçèbazi > baçiçèbazi, çèsézewbame > baçèsézewbame. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with ziba-, ziy-, çèma-, çèba-, zema- or zesé- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix ba- (e.g., zibaqwr > bazizibaqwr, ziyçiçèbal > baziziyçiçèbal, çèmax > baçèçèmax, çèbayrçèsé > baçèçèbayrçèsé, zemawl > bazezemawl, and zeséx > bazezeséx).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with r- change to baàr- (e.g., rçèsézix > baàrçèsézix); those beginning with wqba- or géqba- change to bazeqba- (e.g., wqbaçiçibabemawme > bazeqbaçiçibabemawme, géqbaywqsè > bazeqbaywqsè), with the exception of the irregular géqbayhé (old) whose feminine form is baziziybayhé; l- changes to baql- (e.g., lçèmazi > baqlçèmazi); sèy- changes to bahéy- (e.g., sèyçirsé > bahéyçirsé); sèba- changes to bahéga- (e.g., sèbawx > bahégawx); wba- changes to bawga- (e.g., wbalçèséwçigè > bawgalçèséwçigè); çiba- changes to baçiga- (e.g., çibayqjçèy > baçigayqjçèy); and adjectives beginning with qma- have a special form zima- (becoming bazizima- in feminine) that appears after sé, ba, y, ma, q, f, gè, ga and some occurrences of à, (e.g., qmasè/zimasè > bazizimasè, qmabe/zimabe > bazizimabe).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with ba-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. baàryw babebemaà çèq 'a rich man' > baàryw babebebasè baçèq 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix ze- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., yzimada > zeyzimada, bayzimada > zebayzimada). If the basic form beginning with ze-, gé-, or p-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., zeséx > zeséx, géqbawgèçègèl > géqbawgèçègèl, géqmase > géqmase), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Àrçèbawsè adjectives beginning with qséba- take the prefix gé- in the masculine plural (e.g., qsébahéqmaçè > géqsébahéqmaçè). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with zisé-, which normally change to géqsé- in the masculine plural (e.g., ziséçèwbahéyà > géqséçèwbahéyà, ziséwçiçèbar > géqséwçiçèbar), with only two exceptions: ziséçisésè > zeziséçisésè and ziséhéséçè > zeziséhéséçè which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: baziséwçiçèbar > zebaziséwçiçèbar.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed before the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in balqmaw çèyhé bazi (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically follow their nouns. These are qsébax (beautiful), çèmax (good), sèbawx (brief), seçèséwl (big/tall), zemawl (fat/large), géqsésè (false), çiqséà (high), lçèmazi (long), sèbawx (brief), baçèqbada (young), yzimada (pretty), zeyséhéqsébe (bad), wqbaziziybabe (better), qsébahéqmaçè (new), çiyçibame (small), géqbayhé (old); e.g., babebebasè bazizibax baçèq ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Àrçèbawsè, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
àrçèbawsè personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | bada
         | 2nd (informal)   | qçi
         | 2nd (formal)     | zeqmahé
         | 3rd (masculine)  | ziy
         | 3rd (feminine)   | baziziba
         | 3rd (neutral)    | çèma
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | zeqmaçè
         | 2nd              | zeqmahé
         | 3rd (masculine)  | zeziy
         | 3rd (feminine)   | zebaziziba
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun bada occurs after sé, ba, y, ma, q, f, gè, ga, ê and some occurrences of à, it becomes 'da.

*Relative pronouns

àrçèbawsè, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Àrçèbawsè, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, yqj is ordinarily used: baçiçibazirfryx sébe gèzimahé sé yqj babebemaà'zi ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that yqj in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: zebagèzimahé gèçigè çiçèma yqj zebaçiçibazirfryx zebazi ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, baqj (or 'qj after sé, ba, y, ma, q, f, gè, ga, ê and some occurrences of à) is ordinarily used: bagèzimahé sé ziy'qj baçiçibazirfryx sézi ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like yqj, baqj does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Àrçèbawsè are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Àrçèbawsè is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) wymahésé ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of bawçiê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is bawçiê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is wymahésé. Forms of bawçiê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Àrçèbawsè, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

àrçèbawsè verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -zezey- between the stem and the ending.

    In çiçèbayséziwséme, the stem -ziwséme indicates that the verb is wbaziwséme (to speak) and the prefix çiçèbaysé- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In zeçèmazezeyçèysè, the stem -çèysè indicates that the verb is wyçèysè (to finish), the prefix -zezey- precedes it, and the inflection zeçèma- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Àrçèbawsè they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    wbaziwséme: zeyséwbaziwséme bada, zeséziwséme qçi, çiçèbazezeséziwséme zeziy'qj, zeçèmayziwséme zeqmaçè baqj, pbaziwséme...
    wyçèysè: zeyséwyçèysè bada, zebaçiîçèysè zeqmahé, çiçèbazezeyçèysè zeziy'qj, zeyçèysè, zeçèmayzezeyçèysè zeqmaçè baqj...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    wymaziqmahé: géqbahé bada, géqbahé qçi, çiqbahé ziy, zeçèmaziqmahé zeqmaçè, pbaziqmahé zeqmahé, çiçèbaziqbahé zeziy.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly wymahésé, bawçiê, wbazizisé and bawysésè), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with wba- (with the exception of wbazizisé, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    wbabeysé, wbafséziséx, wbaçiçèséàr, wbafmahéçèba, wbabewbasè, wbalçèsébe, wbazezeséme, wbafséme, wbaçèbabemawme, wbasewsélbaw, etc.

        For example, for the verb wbaziwséme, the stem is -ziwséme and the infinitive prefix is wba-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with wy- whose present participle begins with çiçèsézezey-:

    wyçègèx, wyçisémebemar, wymewbaqlgèse, wywqbazisè, wyseçèséwl, wïséà, wyçizebahéçèy, wyzimame, wylqmaw, wylqw, wyziséze, etc.

        For example, for the verb wyçèysè, the stem is -çèysè and the infinitive prefix is wy-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries bawçiê and wymahésé, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. basewsélbaw bada means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with wba- (all verbs of the first group): ba-, zeba-, ba-, zeçèma-, pba-, çiçèba-.
    Verbs beginning with wy- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): zey-, zey-, çiy-, zeçèmazezey-, pbazezey-, çiçèbazezey-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with baw- (part of the third group): ze-, ze-, - , zeçèma-, pba-, çiçèba-.
    
    Example:

1st Group: wbasewsélbaw (to watch)
-------------------------------
Person         | Singular             | Plural
-------------------------------
1st person     | basewsélbaw bada         | zeçèmasewsélbaw zeqmaçè
2nd person     | zebasewsélbaw qçi        | pbasewsélbaw zeqmahé
3rd person     | basewsélbaw çèma/baziziba/ziy | çiçèbasewsélbaw zebaziziba/zeziy
-------------------------------

2nd Group: wyzeymaàr (to choose)
-------------------------------
Person         | Singular             | Plural
-------------------------------
1st person     | zeyzeymaàr bada         | zeçèmazezeyzeymaàr zeqmaçè
2nd person     | zeyzeymaàr qçi         | pbazezeyzeymaàr zeqmahé
3rd person     | çiyzeymaàr çèma/baziziba/ziy | çiçèbazezeyzeymaàr zebaziziba/zeziy
-------------------------------

-------------------------------
Person         | Singular             | Plural
-------------------------------
1st person     | zeseçèbarzebase bada        | zeçèmaseçèbarzebase zeqmaçè
2nd person     | zeseçèbarzebase qçi        | pbaseçèbarzebase zeqmahé
3rd person     | seçèbarzebase çèma/baziziba/ziy | çiçèbaseçèbarzebase zebaziziba/zeziy
-------------------------------

    Verbs of the second group take an -zezey- in the plural conjugations.
        
        
**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "zeysésewsélbaw bada" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.
    For the first group, the stem is the infinitive minus the wba- prefix, e.g., wbasewsélbaw -> -sewsélbaw.
    For the second group, the stem is the infinitive minus the wy- prefix plus the zezey- prefix, e.g., wyzeymaàr -> -zezeyzeymaàr. 
    And for the third group, the stem is derived from the first person plural of the present indicative.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: zeysé-, zeysé-, çiysé-, zeçèmay-, pbay-, çiçèbaysé-.



    Example:

Person         | Singular               | Plural
-------------------------------
1st person     | zeysésewsélbaw bada         | zeçèmaysewsélbaw zeqmaçè
2nd person     | zeysésewsélbaw qçi         | pbaysewsélbaw zeqmahé
3rd person     | çiysésewsélbaw çèma/baziziba/ziy | çiçèbaysésewsélbaw zebaziziba/zeziy
-------------------------------

2nd Group: wyzeymaàr (to choose)
-------------------------------
Person         | Singular                | Plural
-------------------------------
1st person     | zeysézezeyzeymaàr bada        | zeçèmayzezeyzeymaàr zeqmaçè
2nd person     | zeysézezeyzeymaàr qçi        | pbayzezeyzeymaàr zeqmahé
3rd person     | çiysézezeyzeymaàr çèma/baziziba/ziy | çiçèbaysézezeyzeymaàr zebaziziba/zeziy
-------------------------------



    Verb bawçiê : the stem is -çigè, endings are the same.
    

**Future

The future prefixes correspond to the present indicative of the verb wymahésé. They are always regular: ysé-, zesé-, sé-, zeçèma-, pba-, çiçèma-.

    The future stem is simply the infinitive (dictionary form). In other words, to form the future tense these prefixes are added to the infinitive:

        yséwyzeymaàr bada ('I will choose'), zeséwbasewsélbaw qçi ('you will watch'), séwyçiwmaze baziziba ('she will exit'), zeçèmawbaziziyséhéséwçi zeqmaçè ('we will work'), pbawylqmaw zeqmahé ('you will blush'), çiçèmawyçiwséme zeziy ('they will leave').

    But there are several irregular future stems, especially in the third group.

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding ba- and ze- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. WORD ORDER
----------

The most common word order in Uèhzàgalà is the rare object-verb-subject (OVS).

    kgoézoèzouè zàé zàgazopgo’ni (I love chocolate).

------------------------
ARTICLES AND DETERMINERS 
------------------------
In Uèhzàgalà, articles and determiners are required on almost every common noun, much more so than in English. They are inflected to agree in gender (masculine or feminine) and number (singular or plural) with the noun they determine, though most have only one plural form (for masculine and feminine).

* Articles
uèhzàgalà has three articles: a definite article, corresponding in many cases to English the; an indefinite article, corresponding to English a/an; and a partitive article, used roughly like some in English. 

** Definite article
 	
In Uèhzàgalà, the definite article, analogously to the English word the, is used to indicate a specific noun. However, unlike English, the Uèhzàgalà article changes based on the noun's gender (masculine or feminine) and number (singular or plural).

The definite article always comes after its noun.

For singular nouns:

- For masculine singular nouns, the article is zàé. For example, in the phrase "kgouè zàé" (the cat), zàé shows that the noun kgouè (cat) is both singular and masculine.
- For feminine singular nouns, the article is goé. An example is "hzoyfgono goé" (the house), where goé shows that hzoyfgono (house) is singular and feminine.

For plural nouns, regardless of gender:

- The article is yzàé for both masculine and feminine plural nouns. (e.g., "ykgouè yzàé", the cats; "yhzoyfgono yzàé", the houses.)

In summary, zàé is used with masculine singular nouns, goé with feminine singular nouns, and yzàé with all plural nouns. This variation in definite articles reflects the grammatical gender and number of nouns in Uèhzàgalà.

After go, zà, f, zo, q, sà, jo, v and some occurrences of u, the singular masculine article zàé becomes 'é.


-----
NOUNS
-----
* Gender
Every Uèhzàgalà noun has a grammatical gender, either masculine or feminine.

* Number
As in English, Uèhzàgalà nouns inflect for number, however they do so through prefixation rather than suffixation.

The plural is usually formed from the singular by adding the prefix morpheme ze- (e.g., hzoyfgono > zehzoyfgono 'houses'). 

Nouns beginning with qgo- and qzà- take the prefix y- instead of ze- (e.g., qgosàqk > zeqgosàqk 'pipes', qzàni > zeqzàni 'games'), except for the nouns qgophgoé, qgogagagoy, qzàhtà, and qzàézi which form their plural by prefixing the morpheme y- (e.g., qzàhtà > yqzàhtà 'tires').

Seven nouns beginning with qzo- form their plural with ze-. These are qzohzàm, qzoééfgoè, qzozifu, qzonifzi, qzotà, qzouè, and qzoniqzoni (e.g., qzohzàm > zeqzohzàm 'knees'). All other nouns beginning with qzo-, such as qzoyfzi or qzogak, follow the regular plural pattern and take y- (e.g., qzogak > yqzogak 'holes').

Nouns that begin with y-, ze- or r- in the singular do not change in the plural (e.g., zefzogaè goé 'the cross' > zefzogaè yzàé 'the crosses').

Nouns that begin with égo- typically change to zeqgo- in the plural (e.g., égohgaqzoni > zeqgohgaqzoni 'newspapers'). However, several nouns beginning with égo- are exceptions to this rule and form their plural by adding y- instead. These are égozi, égoè, égodegohgagoè, égoègouè, égodefkyzàlà, égokfèjoga, égodegazày and égomjoga (e.g., égodefkyzàlà zàé > yégodefkyzàlà yzàé).

Similarly, most nouns beginning with éfgo- change to zeqgo- in the plural. Examples of this pattern include éfgozi, éfgogazoè, éfgonojo, éfgogaftàqzoy, éfgodegogak, and éfgogakfde (e.g., éfgogakfde hq > zeqgogakfde yzàp 'stained-glass windows'). However, some éfgo- nouns do not follow this pattern and form their plural with y-, notably éfgoga, éfgogafkkgo, éfgophgouè, éfgokjop, éfgohgazàdeqzom and éfgokgazotà (e.g., éfgoga zàé > yéfgoga yzàé 'the rails').

* Case
Nouns in Uèhzàgalà are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

----------
ADJECTIVES
----------

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Uèhzàgalà adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like qgozàzi and qgozàdeqzoh, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in go, zà, f, zo, q, sà, jo, v and some occurrences of u, e.g. hfpgagoni qgozàzi hq (a beautiful garden), zànonozou ézàzi hq (a handsome man), zànonozàlà zàéézàzi zàhq (a beautiful woman), ykhgolàhzà zeqgozàzi yzàé (the beautiful children), yhzoyfgono yzàéézàzi yzàé (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix zà- to the masculine form, e.g., phgogam > zàphgogam, khzàé > zàkhzàé, hgoygazàtà > zàhgoygazàtà. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with ézà-, éf-, hzo-, hzà-, yzo- or ygo- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix zà- (e.g., ézàqgaè > zàéézàqgaè, éfkhzàm > zàééfkhzàm, hzozi > zàhhzozi, hzàfèhgo > zàhhzàfèhgo, yzogam > zàyyzogam, and ygozi > zàyygozi).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with è- change to zàuè- (e.g., èhgoézi > zàuèhgoézi); those beginning with gaqzà- or zeqzà- change to zàyqzà- (e.g., gaqzàkkzànozogatà > zàyqzàkkzànozogatà, zeqzàfgaqlà > zàyqzàfgaqlà), with the exception of the irregular zeqzàfde (old) whose feminine form is zàééfzàfde; m- changes to zàqm- (e.g., mhzoé > zàqmhzoé); làf- changes to zàdef- (e.g., làfkègo > zàdefkègo); làzà- changes to zàdev- (e.g., làzàgazi > zàdevgazi); gazà- changes to zàgav- (e.g., gazàmhgogakjo > zàgavmhgogakjo); kzà- changes to zàkv- (e.g., kzàfqxhf > zàkvfqxhf); and adjectives beginning with qzo- have a special form ézo- (becoming zàéézo- in feminine) that appears after go, zà, f, zo, q, sà, jo, v and some occurrences of u, (e.g., qzolà/ézolà > zàéézolà, qzono/ézono > zàéézono).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with zà-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. zàuèfga zànonozou hq 'a rich man' > zàuèfga zànonozàlà zàhq 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix y- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., fézoni > yfézoni, zàfézoni > yzàfézoni). If the basic form beginning with y-, ze-, or r-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., ygozi > ygozi, zeqzàgajohjom > zeqzàgajohjom, zeqzop > zeqzop), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Uèhzàgalà adjectives beginning with qgozà- take the prefix ze- in the masculine plural (e.g., qgozàdeqzoh > zeqgozàdeqzoh). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with égo-, which normally change to zeqgo- in the masculine plural (e.g., égohgazàdefu > zeqgohgazàdefu, égogakhzàè > zeqgogakhzàè), with only two exceptions: égokgolà > yégokgolà and égodegoh > yégodegoh which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: zàégogakhzàè > yzàégogakhzàè.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed before the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in zàmqzoga hfde zàé (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically follow their nouns. These are qgozàzi (beautiful), hzozi (good), làzàgazi (brief), phgogam (big/tall), yzogam (fat/large), zeqgolà (false), kqgou (high), mhzoé (long), làzàgazi (brief), zàhqzàni (young), fézoni (pretty), yfgodeqgono (bad), gaqzàééfzàno (better), qgozàdeqzoh (new), kfkzàtà (small), zeqzàfde (old); e.g., zànonozàlà zàéézàzi zàhq ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Uèhzàgalà, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
uèhzàgalà personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | zàni
         | 2nd (informal)   | qk
         | 2nd (formal)     | yqzode
         | 3rd (masculine)  | éf
         | 3rd (feminine)   | zàéézà
         | 3rd (neutral)    | hzo
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | yqzoh
         | 2nd              | yqzode
         | 3rd (masculine)  | yéf
         | 3rd (feminine)   | yzàéézà
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun zàni occurs after go, zà, f, zo, q, sà, jo, v, ê and some occurrences of u, it becomes 'ni.

*Relative pronouns

uèhzàgalà, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Uèhzàgalà, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, fqx is ordinarily used: zàkkzàéèsàèfzi gono joézode go fqx zànonozou'é ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that fqx in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: yzàjoézode jokjo khzo fqx yzàkkzàéèsàèfzi yzàé ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, zàqx (or 'qx after go, zà, f, zo, q, sà, jo, v, ê and some occurrences of u) is ordinarily used: zàjoézode go éf'qx zàkkzàéèsàèfzi goé ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like fqx, zàqx does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Uèhzàgalà are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Uèhzàgalà is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) gafzodego ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of zàgakê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is zàgakê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is gafzodego. Forms of zàgakê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Uèhzàgalà, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

uèhzàgalà verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -yyf- between the stem and the ending.

    In khzàfgoégagotà, the stem -égagotà indicates that the verb is gazàégagotà (to speak) and the prefix khzàfgo- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In yhzoyyfhflà, the stem -hflà indicates that the verb is gafhflà (to finish), the prefix -yyf- precedes it, and the inflection yhzo- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Uèhzàgalà they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    gazàégagotà: yfgogazàégagotà zàni, ygoégagotà qk, khzàyygoégagotà yéf'qx, yhzofégagotà yqzoh zàqx, rzàégagotà...
    gafhflà: yfgogafhflà zàni, yzàkîhflà yqzode, khzàyyfhflà yéf'qx, yfhflà, yhzofyyfhflà yqzoh zàqx...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    gafzoéqzode: zeqzàde zàni, zeqzàde qk, kqzàde éf, yhzoéqzode yqzoh, rzàéqzode yqzode, khzàéqzàde yéf.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly gafzodego, zàgakê, gazàéégo and zàgafgolà), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with gazà- (with the exception of gazàéégo, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    gazànofgo, gazàsàgoégozi, gazàkhgouè, gazàsàzodehzà, gazànogazàlà, gazàmhgono, gazàyygotà, gazàsàgotà, gazàhzànozogatà, gazàpgagomzàga, etc.

        For example, for the verb gazàégagotà, the stem is -égagotà and the infinitive prefix is gazà-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with gaf- whose present participle begins with khgoyyf-:

    gafhjozi, gafkgotànozoè, gaftàgazàqmjop, gafgaqzàélà, gafphgogam, gaïgou, gafkyzàdehf, gafézotà, gafmqzoga, gafmqga, gafégoy, etc.

        For example, for the verb gafhflà, the stem is -hflà and the infinitive prefix is gaf-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries zàgakê and gafzodego, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. zàpgagomzàga zàni means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with gazà- (all verbs of the first group): zà-, yzà-, zà-, yhzo-, rzà-, khzà-.
    Verbs beginning with gaf- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): yf-, yf-, kf-, yhzoyyf-, rzàyyf-, khzàyyf-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with zàga- (part of the third group): y-, y-, - , yhzo-, rzà-, khzà-.
    
    Example:

1st Group: gazàpgagomzàga (to watch)
-------------------------------
Person         | Singular             | Plural
-------------------------------
1st person     | zàpgagomzàga zàni         | yhzopgagomzàga yqzoh
2nd person     | yzàpgagomzàga qk        | rzàpgagomzàga yqzode
3rd person     | zàpgagomzàga hzo/zàéézà/éf | khzàpgagomzàga yzàéézà/yéf
-------------------------------

2nd Group: gafyfzouè (to choose)
-------------------------------
Person         | Singular             | Plural
-------------------------------
1st person     | yfyfzouè zàni         | yhzoyyfyfzouè yqzoh
2nd person     | yfyfzouè qk         | rzàyyfyfzouè yqzode
3rd person     | kfyfzouè hzo/zàéézà/éf | khzàyyfyfzouè yzàéézà/yéf
-------------------------------

-------------------------------
Person         | Singular             | Plural
-------------------------------
1st person     | yphzàèyzàp zàni        | yhzophzàèyzàp yqzoh
2nd person     | yphzàèyzàp qk        | rzàphzàèyzàp yqzode
3rd person     | phzàèyzàp hzo/zàéézà/éf | khzàphzàèyzàp yzàéézà/yéf
-------------------------------

    Verbs of the second group take an -yyf- in the plural conjugations.
        
        
**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "yfgopgagomzàga zàni" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.
    For the first group, the stem is the infinitive minus the gazà- prefix, e.g., gazàpgagomzàga -> -pgagomzàga.
    For the second group, the stem is the infinitive minus the gaf- prefix plus the yyf- prefix, e.g., gafyfzouè -> -yyfyfzouè. 
    And for the third group, the stem is derived from the first person plural of the present indicative.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: yfgo-, yfgo-, kfgo-, yhzof-, rzàf-, khzàfgo-.



    Example:

Person         | Singular               | Plural
-------------------------------
1st person     | yfgopgagomzàga zàni         | yhzofpgagomzàga yqzoh
2nd person     | yfgopgagomzàga qk         | rzàfpgagomzàga yqzode
3rd person     | kfgopgagomzàga hzo/zàéézà/éf | khzàfgopgagomzàga yzàéézà/yéf
-------------------------------

2nd Group: gafyfzouè (to choose)
-------------------------------
Person         | Singular                | Plural
-------------------------------
1st person     | yfgoyyfyfzouè zàni        | yhzofyyfyfzouè yqzoh
2nd person     | yfgoyyfyfzouè qk        | rzàfyyfyfzouè yqzode
3rd person     | kfgoyyfyfzouè hzo/zàéézà/éf | khzàfgoyyfyfzouè yzàéézà/yéf
-------------------------------



    Verb zàgakê : the stem is -kjo, endings are the same.
    

**Future

The future prefixes correspond to the present indicative of the verb gafzodego. They are always regular: fgo-, ygo-, go-, yhzo-, rzà-, khzo-.

    The future stem is simply the infinitive (dictionary form). In other words, to form the future tense these prefixes are added to the infinitive:

        fgogafyfzouè zàni ('I will choose'), ygogazàpgagomzàga qk ('you will watch'), gogafkgazoy zàéézà ('she will exit'), yhzogazàééfgodegogak yqzoh ('we will work'), rzàgafmqzoga yqzode ('you will blush'), khzogafkgagotà yéf ('they will leave').

    But there are several irregular future stems, especially in the third group.

    Example:

**Past participle
