Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with lau-, laq-, ñebè-, ñeu-, xbè- or xma- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix u- (e.g., laukaçyce > ulalaukaçyce, laqrñeuby > ulalaqrñeuby, ñebèðé > uñeñebèðé, ñeuqceñema > uñeñeuqceñema, xbèçyby > uxxbèçyby, and xmaðé > uxxmaðé).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with ce- change to unce- (e.g., ceñemalaðé > unceñemalaðé); those beginning with çykau- or mekau- change to uxkau- (e.g., çykaurruñabèçyv > uxkaurruñabèçyv, mekauqçykag > uxkauqçykag), with the exception of the irregular mekauqo (old) whose feminine form is ulalaquqo; by- changes to ukaby- (e.g., byñebèla > ukabyñebèla); gq- changes to uoq- (e.g., gqrcema > uoqrcema); gu- changes to uoðe- (e.g., guçyðé > uoðeçyðé); çyu- changes to uçyðe- (e.g., çyubyñemaçyrké > uçyðebyñemaçyrké); ru- changes to urðe- (e.g., ruqkaçeñeq > urðeqkaçeñeq); and adjectives beginning with kabè- have a special form labè- (becoming ulalabè- in feminine) that appears after ma, u, q, bè, ka, lé, ké, ðe and some occurrences of n, (e.g., kabèg/labèg > ulalabèg, kabèña/labèña > ulalabèña).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with u-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. unceqçy uñañabèn ñeka 'a rich man' > unceqçy uñañaug uñeka 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix x- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., qlabès > xqlabès, uqlabès > xuqlabès). If the basic form beginning with x-, me-, or à-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., xmaðé > xmaðé, mekauçykéñekéby > mekauçykéñekéby, mekabèz > mekabèz), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Nceñeuçyg adjectives beginning with kamau- take the prefix me- in the masculine plural (e.g., kamauokabèñe > mekamauokabèñe). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with lama-, which normally change to mekama- in the masculine plural (e.g., lamañeçyuoqn > mekamañeçyuoqn, lamaçyrñeuce > mekamaçyrñeuce), with only two exceptions: lamarmag > xlamarmag and lamaomañe > xlamaomañe which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: ulamaçyrñeuce > xulamaçyrñeuce.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed before the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in ubykabèçy ñeqo ula (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically follow their nouns. These are kamauðé (beautiful), ñebèðé (good), guçyðé (brief), zñemaçyby (big/tall), xbèçyby (fat/large), mekamag (false), rkaman (high), byñebèla (long), guçyðé (brief), uñekaus (young), qlabès (pretty), xqmaokamaña (bad), çykaulalaquña (better), kamauokabèñe (new), rqruv (small), mekauqo (old); e.g., uñañaug ulalauðé uñeka ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Nceñeuçyg, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
nceñeuçyg personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | us
         | 2nd (informal)   | kar
         | 2nd (formal)     | xkabèo
         | 3rd (masculine)  | laq
         | 3rd (feminine)   | ulalau
         | 3rd (neutral)    | ñebè
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | xkabèñe
         | 2nd              | xkabèo
         | 3rd (masculine)  | xlaq
         | 3rd (feminine)   | xulalau
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun us occurs after ma, u, q, bè, ka, lé, ké, ðe, ê and some occurrences of n, it becomes 's.

*Relative pronouns

nceñeuçyg, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Nceñeuçyg, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, qkaçe is ordinarily used: urrulaceléceqðé maña kélabèo ma qkaçe uñañabèn'la ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that qkaçe in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: xukélabèo kérké rñebè qkaçe xurrulaceléceqðé xula ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, ukaçe (or 'kaçe after ma, u, q, bè, ka, lé, ké, ðe, ê and some occurrences of n) is ordinarily used: ukélabèo ma laq'kaçe urrulaceléceqðé mala ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like qkaçe, ukaçe does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Nceñeuçyg are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Nceñeuçyg is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) çyqbèoma ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of uçyrê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is uçyrê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is çyqbèoma. Forms of uçyrê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Nceñeuçyg, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

nceñeuçyg verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -xxq- between the stem and the ending.

    In rñeuqmalaçymav, the stem -laçymav indicates that the verb is çyulaçymav (to speak) and the prefix rñeuqma- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In xñebèxxqñeqg, the stem -ñeqg indicates that the verb is çyqñeqg (to finish), the prefix -xxq- precedes it, and the inflection xñebè- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Nceñeuçyg they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    çyulaçymav: xqmaçyulaçymav us, xmalaçymav kar, rñeuxxmalaçymav xlaq'kaçe, xñebèqlaçymav xkabèñe ukaçe, àulaçymav...
    çyqñeqg: xqmaçyqñeqg us, xurîñeqg xkabèo, rñeuxxqñeqg xlaq'kaçe, xqñeqg, xñebèqxxqñeqg xkabèñe ukaçe...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    çyqbèlakabèo: mekauo us, mekauo kar, rkauo laq, xñebèlakabèo xkabèñe, àulakabèo xkabèo, rñeulakauo xlaq.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly çyqbèoma, uçyrê, çyulalama and uçyqmag), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with çyu- (with the exception of çyulalama, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    çyuñaqma, çyulémalamaðé, çyurñemance, çyulébèoñeu, çyuñaçyug, çyubyñemaña, çyuxxmav, çyulémav, çyuñeuñabèçyv, çyuzçymabyuçy, etc.

        For example, for the verb çyulaçymav, the stem is -laçymav and the infinitive prefix is çyu-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with çyq- whose present participle begins with rñemaxxq-:

    çyqñekéðé, çyqrmavñabèce, çyqvçyukabykéz, çyqçykaulag, çyqzñemaçyby, çyïman, çyqrxuoñeq, çyqlabèv, çyqbykabèçy, çyqbykaçy, çyqlamax, etc.

        For example, for the verb çyqñeqg, the stem is -ñeqg and the infinitive prefix is çyq-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries uçyrê and çyqbèoma, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. uzçymabyuçy us means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with çyu- (all verbs of the first group): u-, xu-, u-, xñebè-, àu-, rñeu-.
    Verbs beginning with çyq- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): xq-, xq-, rq-, xñebèxxq-, àuxxq-, rñeuxxq-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with uçy- (part of the third group): x-, x-, - , xñebè-, àu-, rñeu-.
    
    Example:

-------------------------------

2nd person     | xuzçymabyuçy kar        | àuzçymabyuçy xkabèo
3rd person     | uzçymabyuçy ñebè/ulalau/laq | rñeuzçymabyuçy xulalau/xlaq
-------------------------------

2nd person     | xqxqbènce kar         | àuxxqxqbènce xkabèo

**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "xqmazçymabyuçy us" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.
    For the first group, the stem is the infinitive minus the çyu- prefix, e.g., çyuzçymabyuçy -> -zçymabyuçy.
    For the second group, the stem is the infinitive minus the çyq- prefix plus the xxq- prefix, e.g., çyqxqbènce -> -xxqxqbènce. 
    And for the third group, the stem is derived from the first person plural of the present indicative.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: xqma-, xqma-, rqma-, xñebèq-, àuq-, rñeuqma-.

**Future

The future prefixes correspond to the present indicative of the verb çyqbèoma. They are always regular: qma-, xma-, ma-, xñebè-, àu-, rñebè-.

    The future stem is simply the infinitive (dictionary form). In other words, to form the future tense these prefixes are added to the infinitive:

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding u- and x- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "rqgñebèce rqkaçyg ñeka", "urqgñebèce uçyqbèv uñeka", "xrqgñebèce xrqkaçyg xuz", and "xurqgñebèce xuçyqbèv xuz."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with ké- for the 1st group verbs, and with q- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : ka- (uçyzñeurñeu kazñeurñeu, uçyqbèðé kaðé, uçyqla kala, etc. and çyqbèomax kax, çyqbèo kao, çyqbèokabèv kav), xq- (uçyrruña xqña, uçyzñeuçyv xqçyv, etc.), xka- (uçykalaceñeq xkalaceñeq and uçykalaceuçy xkalaceuçy and only these verbs), rq- (uçyqzkamaña rqzkamaña, uçyqz rqz, etc.), r- (verbs in uçyzñeq- : uçyzñequv rñequv), rçyu- (çyqçyokabè rçyuokabè, çyqçyokabèce rçyuokabèce, çyqçyggbè rçyuggbè and çyqçyggkabèx rçyuggkabèx), or kau (çyqbèoma kau). 

*Compound Tenses

nceñeuçyg compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either çyqbèoma or uçyrê) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Nceñeuçyg, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Nceñeuçyg. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either çyqbèoma or uçyrê in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "kébyñemaña qma's" (I ate) or "kéoqçyçyma rxu laq" (He arrived). çyqbèoma is used with most verbs, while uçyrê is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, çyqbèoma should be used by default.

*Past participle agreement

The past participle is used in three ways in Nceñeuçyg: as an adjective, in the passive construction, and in the compound tense constructions. When it is used as an adjective, it follows all the regular adjective agreement rules. In passive constructions, it always agrees with the passive subject.

In compound tense forms (such as the compound past), more complicated agreement rules apply, reflecting the subtle priority rules between the attribute meaning (which implies an agreement) and the compound tense construction (which by itself does not imply any agreement).

A. The auxiliary verb is çyqbèoma.

    If there is no direct object (the verb is intransitive) or the direct object appears before the past participle, then the past participle does not agree (i.e., it takes the default masculine singular form).
        (intransitive) qñaçybèz rñebè xulalau. ("They (fem.) slept.")
        (direct object before verb) xuñequlamaðé mekauz kao ma uçyqmalace. ("uçyqmalace saw two whales.")
    If there is a direct object and it appears after the past participle, then the participle must agree with it. Three cases:
        (pronoun after the auxiliary) xuñequlamaðé mekauz rqmaoma lé laq. xukao ma xula uçyqmalace. ("There were two whales. uçyqmalace saw them.")
        (clause-final wh-question element)  xukao ulalau-r-ma uçyqmalace xuñequlamaðé xulalaukaçe? ("Which whales did uçyqmalace see?")
        (relative clause linked by ukaçe) xukao ma uçyqmalace ukaçe xuñequlamaðé mekauz xula ("the two whales that uçyqmalace saw")
    The above rule is one of the most difficult in Nceñeuçyg.

They are inflected to agree in gender (masculine or feminine) and number (singular or plural) with the noun they determine, though most have only one plural form (for masculine and feminine).

* Articles
pþoþucbov has three articles: a definite article, corresponding in many cases to English the; an indefinite article, corresponding to English a/an; and a partitive article, used roughly like some in English. 

** Definite article
 	
In Pþoþucbov, the definite article, analogously to the English word the, is used to indicate a specific noun. However, unlike English, the Pþoþucbov article changes based on the noun's gender (masculine or feminine) and number (singular or plural).

The definite article always comes after its noun.

For singular nouns:

- For masculine singular nouns, the article is cj. For example, in the phrase "hozøpþo cj" (the cat), cj shows that the noun hozøpþo (cat) is both singular and masculine.
- For feminine singular nouns, the article is zøj. An example is "þuétgzøð zøj" (the house), where zøj shows that þuétgzøð (house) is singular and feminine.

For plural nouns, regardless of gender:

- The article is tcj for both masculine and feminine plural nouns. (e.g., "thozøpþo tcj", the cats; "tþuétgzøð tcj", the houses.)

In summary, cj is used with masculine singular nouns, zøj with feminine singular nouns, and tcj with all plural nouns. This variation in definite articles reflects the grammatical gender and number of nouns in Pþoþucbov.

After zø, c, g, é, bè, ê, w, nu and some occurrences of p, the singular masculine article cj becomes 'j.

* Gender
Every Pþoþucbov noun has a grammatical gender, either masculine or feminine.

* Number
As in English, Pþoþucbov nouns inflect for number, however they do so through prefixation rather than suffixation.

The plural is usually formed from the singular by adding the prefix morpheme à- (e.g., þuétgzøð > àþuétgzøð 'houses'). 

Nouns beginning with bèzø- and bèc- take the prefix t- instead of à- (e.g., bèzøêbèho > àbèzøêbèho 'pipes', bècqè > àbècqè 'games'), except for the nouns bèzørûþuzøj, bèzøbobozøt, bècþue, and bècjî which form their plural by prefixing the morpheme t- (e.g., bècþue > tbècþue 'tires').

Nouns that begin with jzø- typically change to àbèzø- in the plural (e.g., jzøþubobèéqè > àbèzøþubobèéqè 'newspapers'). * Case
Nouns in Pþoþucbov are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

ADJECTIVES
----------

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Pþoþucbov adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like bèzøcî and bèzøcnobèéþu, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in zø, c, g, é, bè, ê, w, nu and some occurrences of p, e.g. þugrûbozøqè bèzøcî þubè (a beautiful garden), cððép jcî þubè (a handsome man), cððcv cjjcî cþubè (a beautiful woman), thoþuzøvþuc àbèzøcî tcj (the beautiful children), tþuétgzøð tcjjcî tcj (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix c- to the masculine form, e.g., rûþuzøboç > crûþuzøboç, hoþucj > choþucj, þuzøtboce > cþuzøtboce. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with jc-, jg-, þué-, þuc-, té- or tzø- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix c- (e.g., jcbèboþo > cjjcbèboþo, jghoþucç > cjjghoþucç, þuéî > cþuþuéî, þucgþoþuzø > cþuþucgþoþuzø, téboç > cttéboç, and tzøî > cttzøî).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with þo- change to cpþo- (e.g., þoþuzøjî > cpþoþuzøjî); those beginning with bobèc- or àbèc- change to ctbèc- (e.g., bobèchohocðéboe > ctbèchohocðéboe, àbècgbobèv > ctbècgbobèv), with the exception of the irregular àbècgno (old) whose feminine form is cjjgcgno; ç- changes to cbèç- (e.g., çþuéj > cbèçþuéj); vg- changes to cnog- (e.g., vghoþozø > cnoghoþozø); vc- changes to cnonu- (e.g., vcboî > cnonuboî); boc- changes to cbonu- (e.g., bocçþuzøbohow > cbonuçþuzøbohow); hoc- changes to chonu- (e.g., hocgbèbûþug > chonugbèbûþug); and adjectives beginning with bèé- have a special form jé- (becoming cjjé- in feminine) that appears after zø, c, g, é, bè, ê, w, nu and some occurrences of p, (e.g., bèév/jév > cjjév, bèéð/jéð > cjjéð).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with c-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. cpþogbo cððép þubè 'a rich man' > cpþogbo cððcv cþubè 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix t- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., gjéqè > tgjéqè, cgjéqè > tcgjéqè). If the basic form beginning with t-, à-, or ñ-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., tzøî > tzøî, àbècbowþuwç > àbècbowþuwç, àbèérû > àbèérû), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Pþoþucbov adjectives beginning with bèzøc- take the prefix à- in the masculine plural (e.g., bèzøcnobèéþu > àbèzøcnobèéþu). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with jzø-, which normally change to àbèzø- in the masculine plural (e.g., jzøþubocnogp > àbèzøþubocnogp, jzøbohoþucþo > àbèzøbohoþucþo), with only two exceptions: jzøhozøv > tjzøhozøv and jzønozøþu > tjzønozøþu which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: cjzøbohoþucþo > tcjzøbohoþucþo.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed before the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in cçbèébo þugno cj (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically follow their nouns. PRONOUNS
--------
In Pþoþucbov, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
pþoþucbov personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows:

         | 2nd (formal)     | tbèéno
         | 3rd (masculine)  | jg
         | 3rd (feminine)   | cjjc
         | 3rd (neutral)    | þué
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | tbèéþu
         | 2nd              | tbèéno
         | 3rd (masculine)  | tjg

------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun cqè occurs after zø, c, g, é, bè, ê, w, nu, k and some occurrences of p, it becomes 'qè.

*Relative pronouns

pþoþucbov, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Pþoþucbov, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, gbèbû is ordinarily used: chohocjþoêþogî zøð wjéno zø gbèbû cððép'j ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that gbèbû in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: tcwjéno whow hoþué gbèbû tchohocjþoêþogî tcj ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, cbèbû (or 'bèbû after zø, c, g, é, bè, ê, w, nu, k and some occurrences of p) is ordinarily used: cwjéno zø jg'bèbû chohocjþoêþogî zøj ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like gbèbû, cbèbû does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Pþoþucbov are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Pþoþucbov is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) bogénozø ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of cbohok ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is cbohok, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is bogénozø. Forms of cbohok are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Pþoþucbov, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

pþoþucbov verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -ttg- between the stem and the ending.

    In hoþucgzøjbozøe, the stem -jbozøe indicates that the verb is bocjbozøe (to speak) and the prefix hoþucgzø- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In tþuéttgþugv, the stem -þugv indicates that the verb is bogþugv (to finish), the prefix -ttg- precedes it, and the inflection tþué- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Pþoþucbov they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    bocjbozøe: tgzøbocjbozøe cqè, tzøjbozøe bèho, hoþucttzøjbozøe tjg'bèbû, tþuégjbozøe tbèéþu cbèbû, ñcjbozøe...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    bogéjbèéno: àbècno cqè, àbècno bèho, hobècno jg, tþuéjbèéno tbèéþu, ñcjbèéno tbèéno, hoþucjbècno tjg.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly bogénozø, cbohok, bocjjzø and cbogzøv), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with boc- (with the exception of bocjjzø, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    bocðgzø, bocêzøjzøî, bochoþuzøpþo, bocêénoþuc, bocðbocv, bocçþuzøð, bocttzøe, bocêzøe, bocþucðéboe, bocrûbozøçcbo, etc.

        For example, for the verb bocjbozøe, the stem is -jbozøe and the infinitive prefix is boc-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with bog- whose present participle begins with hoþuzøttg-:

        For example, for the verb bogþugv, the stem is -þugv and the infinitive prefix is bog-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries cbohok and bogénozø, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately.

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Øxeboàilâ adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix à- to the masculine form, e.g., axocilet > àaxocilet, aboàat > àaboàat, ocajilàû > àocajilàû. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with atà-, ats-, oy-, oà-, ajy- or ajc- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix à- (e.g., atàævileb > àatatàævileb, atsaboàet > àatatsaboàet, oyex > àooyex, oàseboc > àooàseboc, ajyilet > àajajyilet, and ajcex > àajajcex).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with eb- change to àøxeb- (e.g., ebocatex > àøxebocatex); those beginning with ilævà- or îævà- change to àajævà- (e.g., ilævàababàqyilû > àajævàababàqyilû, îævàsilævâ > àajævàsilævâ), with the exception of the irregular îævàsav (old) whose feminine form is àatatsàsav; et- changes to àævet- (e.g., etoyat > àævetoyat); âs- changes to àavs- (e.g., âsabebc > àavsabebc); âà- changes to àavf- (e.g., âàilex > àavfilex); ilà- changes to àilf- (e.g., ilàetocilabij > àilfetocilabij); abà- changes to àabf- (e.g., abàsævwos > àabfsævwos); and adjectives beginning with ævy- have a special form aty- (becoming àataty- in feminine) that appears after c, à, s, y, æv, im, ij, f and some occurrences of øx, (e.g., ævyâ/atyâ > àatatyâ, ævyq/atyq > àatatyq).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with à-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. àøxebsil àqqyøx oæv 'a rich man' > àøxebsil àqqàâ àoæv 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix aj- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., satyip > ajsatyip, àsatyip > ajàsatyip). If the basic form beginning with aj-, î-, or am-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., ajcex > ajcex, îævàilijoijet > îævàilijoijet, îævyax > îævyax), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Øxeboàilâ adjectives beginning with ævcà- take the prefix î- in the masculine plural (e.g., ævcàavævyo > îævcàavævyo). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with atc-, which normally change to îævc- in the masculine plural (e.g., atcoilàavsøx > îævcoilàavsøx, atcilaboàeb > îævcilaboàeb), with only two exceptions: atcabcâ > ajatcabcâ and atcavco > ajatcavco which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: àatcilaboàeb > ajàatcilaboàeb.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed before the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in àetævyil osav àat (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically follow their nouns. These are ævcàex (beautiful), oyex (good), âàilex (brief), axocilet (big/tall), ajyilet (fat/large), îævcâ (false), abævcøx (high), etoyat (long), âàilex (brief), àoævàip (young), satyip (pretty), ajscavævcq (bad), ilævàatatsàq (better), ævcàavævyo (new), absabàû (small), îævàsav (old); e.g., àqqàâ àatatàex àoæv ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Øxeboàilâ, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
øxeboàilâ personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | àip
         | 2nd (informal)   | ævab
         | 2nd (formal)     | ajævyav
         | 3rd (masculine)  | ats
         | 3rd (feminine)   | àatatà
         | 3rd (neutral)    | oy
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | ajævyo
         | 2nd              | ajævyav
         | 3rd (masculine)  | ajats
         | 3rd (feminine)   | ajàatatà
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun àip occurs after c, à, s, y, æv, im, ij, f, œ and some occurrences of øx, it becomes 'ip.

*Relative pronouns

øxeboàilâ, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Øxeboàilâ, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, sævw is ordinarily used: àababàatebimebsex cq ijatyav c sævw àqqyøx'at ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that sævw in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: ajàijatyav ijabij aboy sævw ajàababàatebimebsex ajàat ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, àævw (or 'ævw after c, à, s, y, æv, im, ij, f, œ and some occurrences of øx) is ordinarily used: àijatyav c ats'ævw àababàatebimebsex cat ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like sævw, àævw does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Øxeboàilâ are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Øxeboàilâ is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) ilsyavc ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of àilabœ ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is àilabœ, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is ilsyavc. Forms of àilabœ are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Øxeboàilâ, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

øxeboàilâ verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -ajajs- between the stem and the ending.

    In aboàscatilcû, the stem -atilcû indicates that the verb is ilàatilcû (to speak) and the prefix aboàsc- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In ajoyajajsosâ, the stem -osâ indicates that the verb is ilsosâ (to finish), the prefix -ajajs- precedes it, and the inflection ajoy- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Øxeboàilâ they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    ilàatilcû: ajscilàatilcû àip, ajcatilcû ævab, aboàajajcatilcû ajats'ævw, ajoysatilcû ajævyo àævw, amàatilcû...
    ilsosâ: ajscilsosâ àip, ajàabeposâ ajævyav, aboàajajsosâ ajats'ævw, ajsosâ, ajoysajajsosâ ajævyo àævw...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    ilsyatævyav: îævàav àip, îævàav ævab, abævàav ats, ajoyatævyav ajævyo, amàatævyav ajævyav, aboàatævàav ajats.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly ilsyavc, àilabœ, ilàatatc and àilscâ), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with ilà- (with the exception of ilàatatc, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    ilàqsc, ilàimcatcex, ilàabocøxeb, ilàimyavoà, ilàqilàâ, ilàetocq, ilàajajcû, ilàimcû, ilàoàqyilû, ilàaxilcetàil, etc.

        For example, for the verb ilàatilcû, the stem is -atilcû and the infinitive prefix is ilà-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with ils- whose present participle begins with abocajajs-:

    ilsoijex, ilsabcûqyeb, ilsûilàævetijax, ilsilævàatâ, ilsaxocilet, ilïcøx, ilsabajàavos, ilsatyû, ilsetævyil, ilsetævil, ilsatcaj, etc.

        For example, for the verb ilsosâ, the stem is -osâ and the infinitive prefix is ils-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries àilabœ and ilsyavc, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. àaxilcetàil àip means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with ilà- (all verbs of the first group): à-, ajà-, à-, ajoy-, amà-, aboà-.
    Verbs beginning with ils- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): ajs-, ajs-, abs-, ajoyajajs-, amàajajs-, aboàajajs-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with àil- (part of the third group): aj-, aj-, - , ajoy-, amà-, aboà-.

**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "ajscaxilcetàil àip" means "I was watching".

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding à- and aj- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "absâoyeb absævilâ oæv", "àabsâoyeb àilsyû àoæv", "ajabsâoyeb ajabsævilâ ajàax", and "ajàabsâoyeb ajàilsyû ajàax."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with ij- for the 1st group verbs, and with s- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : æv- (àilaxoàaboà ævaxoàaboà, àilsyex ævex, àilsat ævat, etc. and ilsyavcaj ævaj, ilsyav ævav, ilsyavævyû ævû), ajs- (àilababàq ajsq, àilaxoàilû ajsilû, etc.), ajæv- (àilævatebos ajævatebos and àilævatebàil ajævatebàil and only these verbs), abs- (àilsaxævcq absaxævcq, àilsax absax, etc.), ab- (verbs in àilaxos- : àilaxosàû abosàû), abilà- (ilsilavævy abilàavævy, ilsilavævyeb abilàavævyeb, ilsilâây abilàâây and ilsilââævyaj abilàââævyaj), or ævà (ilsyavc ævà). 

*Compound Tenses

øxeboàilâ compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either ilsyavc or àilabœ) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Øxeboàilâ, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Øxeboàilâ. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either ilsyavc or àilabœ in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "ijetocq sc'ip" (I ate) or "ijavsililc abajà ats" (He arrived). ilsyavc is used with most verbs, while àilabœ is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, ilsyavc should be used by default.

*Past participle agreement

The past participle is used in three ways in Øxeboàilâ: as an adjective, in the passive construction, and in the compound tense constructions. When it is used as an adjective, it follows all the regular adjective agreement rules. In passive constructions, it always agrees with the passive subject.

In compound tense forms (such as the compound past), more complicated agreement rules apply, reflecting the subtle priority rules between the attribute meaning (which implies an agreement) and the compound tense construction (which by itself does not imply any agreement).

A. The auxiliary verb is ilsyavc.

    If there is no direct object (the verb is intransitive) or the direct object appears before the past participle, then the past participle does not agree (i.e., it takes the default masculine singular form).
        (intransitive) sqilyax aboy ajàatatà. ("They (fem.) slept.")
        (direct object before verb) ajàosàatcex îævàax ævav c àilscateb. ("àilscateb saw two whales.")
    If there is a direct object and it appears after the past participle, then the participle must agree with it. Three cases:
        (pronoun after the auxiliary) ajàosàatcex îævàax abscavc im ats. ajàævav c ajàat àilscateb. ("There were two whales. àilscateb saw them.")
        (clause-final wh-question element)  ajàævav àatatà-ab-c àilscateb ajàosàatcex ajàatatàævw? ("Which whales did àilscateb see?")
        (relative clause linked by àævw) ajàævav c àilscateb àævw ajàosàatcex îævàax ajàat ("the two whales that àilscateb saw")
    The above rule is one of the most difficult in Øxeboàilâ.

B. The auxiliary is àilabœ, and the verb is not reflexive. The past participle agrees with the subject:

        ajàijavsililc aboyaj ajàatatà. ("They (fem.) arrived.")

These are qomérébo (beautiful), képbo (good), lréybo (brief), hkéméydo (big/tall), àpydo (fat/large), kuqomél (false), gqoméru (high), doképmi (long), lréybo (brief), rékéqorédi (young), bémipdi (pretty), àbémésiqomésu (bad), yqorémimibérésu (better), qomérésiqopké (new), gbégréx (small), kuqorébési (old); e.g., résusurél rémimirébo rékéqo ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Rutkéréyl, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
rutkéréyl personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | rédi
         | 2nd (informal)   | qog
         | 2nd (formal)     | àqopsi
         | 3rd (masculine)  | mibé
         | 3rd (feminine)   | rémimiré
         | 3rd (neutral)    | kép
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | àqopké
         | 2nd              | àqopsi
         | 3rd (masculine)  | àmibé
         | 3rd (feminine)   | àrémimiré
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun rédi occurs after mé, ré, bé, p, qo, çé, w, qi, ê and some occurrences of ru, it becomes 'di.

*Relative pronouns

rutkéréyl, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Rutkéréyl, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, béqov is ordinarily used: réggrémitçétbébo mésu wmipsi mé béqov résusupru'mi ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that béqov in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: àréwmipsi wgw gkép béqov àréggrémitçétbébo àrémi ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, réqov (or 'qov after mé, ré, bé, p, qo, çé, w, qi, ê and some occurrences of ru) is ordinarily used: réwmipsi mé mibé'qov réggrémitçétbébo mémi ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like béqov, réqov does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Rutkéréyl are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Rutkéréyl is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) ybépsimé ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of réygê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is réygê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is ybépsimé. Forms of réygê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Rutkéréyl, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

rutkéréyl verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -ààbé- between the stem and the ending.

    In gkérébémémiyméx, the stem -miyméx indicates that the verb is yrémiyméx (to speak) and the prefix gkérébémé- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In àképààbékébél, the stem -kébél indicates that the verb is ybékébél (to finish), the prefix -ààbé- precedes it, and the inflection àkép- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Rutkéréyl they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    yrémiyméx: àbéméyrémiyméx rédi, àmémiyméx qog, gkéréààmémiyméx àmibé'qov, àképbémiyméx àqopké réqov, frémiyméx...
    ybékébél: àbéméybékébél rédi, àrégîkébél àqopsi, gkéréààbékébél àmibé'qov, àbékébél, àképbéààbékébél àqopké réqov...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    ybépmiqopsi: kuqorési rédi, kuqorési qog, gqorési mibé, àképmiqopsi àqopké, frémiqopsi àqopsi, gkérémiqorési àmibé.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly ybépsimé, réygê, yrémimimé and réybémél), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with yré- (with the exception of yrémimimé, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    yrésubémé, yréçémémimébo, yrégkémérut, yréçépsikéré, yrésuyrél, yrédokémésu, yréààméx, yréçéméx, yrékérésupyx, yréhymédoréy, etc.

        For example, for the verb yrémiyméx, the stem is -miyméx and the infinitive prefix is yré-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with ybé- whose present participle begins with gkéméààbé-:

    ybékéwbo, ybégméxsupt, ybéxyréqodowh, ybéyqorémil, ybéhkéméydo, yïméru, ybégàrésikébé, ybémipx, ybédoqopy, ybédoqoy, ybémiméà, etc.

        For example, for the verb ybékébél, the stem is -kébél and the infinitive prefix is ybé-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries réygê and ybépsimé, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. réhymédoréy rédi means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with yré- (all verbs of the first group): ré-, àré-, ré-, àkép-, fré-, gkéré-.
    Verbs beginning with ybé- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): àbé-, àbé-, gbé-, àképààbé-, fréààbé-, gkéréààbé-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with réy- (part of the third group): à-, à-, - , àkép-, fré-, gkéré-.

**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "àbéméhymédoréy rédi" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding ré- and à- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "gbélképt gbéqoyl kéqo", "régbélképt réybépx rékéqo", "àgbélképt àgbéqoyl àréh", and "àrégbélképt àréybépx àréh."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with w- for the 1st group verbs, and with bé- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : qo- (réyhkérégkéré qohkérégkéré, réybépbo qobo, réybémi qomi, etc. and ybépsiméà qoà, ybépsi qosi, ybépsiqopx qox), àbé- (réyggrésu àbésu, réyhkéréyx àbéyx, etc.), àqo- (réyqomitkébé àqomitkébé and réyqomitréy àqomitréy and only these verbs), gbé- (réybéhqomésu gbéhqomésu, réybéh gbéh, etc.), g- (verbs in réyhkébé- : réyhkébéréx gkébéréx), gyré- (ybéysiqop gyrésiqop, ybéysiqopt gyrésiqopt, ybéyllp gyréllp and ybéyllqopà gyréllqopà), or qoré (ybépsimé qoré). 

*Compound Tenses

rutkéréyl compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either ybépsimé or réygê) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Rutkéréyl, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Rutkéréyl. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either ybépsimé or réygê in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "wdokémésu bémé'di" (I ate) or "wsibéyymé gàré mibé" (He arrived). ybépsimé is used with most verbs, while réygê is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, ybépsimé should be used by default.

*Past participle agreement

The past participle is used in three ways in Rutkéréyl: as an adjective, in the passive construction, and in the compound tense constructions. When it is used as an adjective, it follows all the regular adjective agreement rules. In passive constructions, it always agrees with the passive subject.

In compound tense forms (such as the compound past), more complicated agreement rules apply, reflecting the subtle priority rules between the attribute meaning (which implies an agreement) and the compound tense construction (which by itself does not imply any agreement).

A. The auxiliary verb is ybépsimé.

    If there is no direct object (the verb is intransitive) or the direct object appears before the past participle, then the past participle does not agree (i.e., it takes the default masculine singular form).
        (intransitive) bésuyph gkép àrémimiré. ("They (fem.) slept.")
        (direct object before verb) àrékébérémimébo kuqoréh qosi mé réybémémit. ("réybémémit saw two whales.")
    If there is a direct object and it appears after the past participle, then the participle must agree with it. Three cases:
        (pronoun after the auxiliary) àrékébérémimébo kuqoréh gbémésimé çé mibé. àréqosi mé àrémi réybémémit. ("There were two whales. réybémémit saw them.")
        (clause-final wh-question element)  àréqosi rémimiré-g-mé réybémémit àrékébérémimébo àrémimiréqov? ("Which whales did réybémémit see?")
        (relative clause linked by réqov) àréqosi mé réybémémit réqov àrékébérémimébo kuqoréh àrémi ("the two whales that réybémémit saw")
    The above rule is one of the most difficult in Rutkéréyl.

B. The auxiliary is réygê, and the verb is not reflexive. The past participle agrees with the subject:

        àréwsibéyymé gképà àrémimiré. ("They (fem.) arrived.")

C. The auxiliary is réygê and the verb is reflexive. The agreement rules are in fact the same as those for structures with ybépsimé in A, keeping in mind that the reflexive pronoun corresponds to either the direct object or the indirect object of the verb.

    There is no direct object, or the direct object appears before the past participle → no agreement. In these cases, the reflexive pronoun expresses the indirect object.
        (no direct object) whwttqoà gképà réà àrémimiré. wmiyméx àrésusupà àqopké àqopké. ("They (fem.) succeeded one another. We spoke with each other.")
        (direct object before verb) àképbégàréqov àréh wàpx gképà réà àrémimiré. ("They (fem.) asked each other some questions.")
        
    There is a direct object and it appears after the past participle. → The past participle agrees with this object.

    The first three cases are the same as in A.2 above (the reflexive pronoun is the indirect object).
        (direct object pronoun) régymég rékéqo gbémél bémé'di. réwdomégyméx gképà mémi réà àgkémélkéré àrémi. ("I made a pie. The children shared it.")
        (wh-question)  réwdomégyméx àmibé-gképà réà régymég rémimiréqov? ("Which pie did they share?")
        (réqov relative) réwdomégyméx gképà réà àgkémélkéré àrémi réqov régymég mémi ("the pie that the children shared")

    The reflexive pronoun can itself be the direct object, in which case the participle agrees with it (and therefore with the subject). This also includes "inherently reflexive" verbs, for which the reflexive pronoun cannot be interpreted semantically as an object (direct or indirect) of the verb.
        (ordinary reflexive) àrébésibéqoà gképà réà àrémimiré. àwqomiméà àrésusupà àqopké àqopké. ("They (fem.) followed each other. We greeted each other.")
        (inherently reflexive) bépsu réh àwqovpsu gképà réà àmibé. gkérésurékéwsiw'mi réh àqokérésiqopà àrésusupà àqopké àqopké. ("They made fun of me. We remembered the event.")

Beginning of Idbqipèhj Grammar Book Excerpts

----------
WORD ORDER
----------

The most common word order in Idbqipèhj is the rare object-verb-subject (OVS).

    léemepbepidb ipem ipèhepavé’èd (I love chocolate).

------------------------
ARTICLES AND DETERMINERS 
------------------------
In Idbqipèhj, articles and determiners are required on almost every common noun, much more so than in English. They are inflected to agree in gender (masculine or feminine) and number (singular or plural) with the noun they determine, though most have only one plural form (for masculine and feminine).

* Articles
idbqipèhj has three articles: a definite article, corresponding in many cases to English the; an indefinite article, corresponding to English a/an; and a partitive article, used roughly like some in English. 

** Definite article
 	
In Idbqipèhj, the definite article, analogously to the English word the, is used to indicate a specific noun. However, unlike English, the Idbqipèhj article changes based on the noun's gender (masculine or feminine) and number (singular or plural).

The definite article always comes after its noun.

For singular nouns:

- For masculine singular nouns, the article is ipem. For example, in the phrase "léidb ipem" (the cat), ipem shows that the noun léidb (cat) is both singular and masculine.
- For feminine singular nouns, the article is éem. An example is "qepçanéyp éem" (the house), where éem shows that qepçanéyp (house) is singular and feminine.

For plural nouns, regardless of gender:

- The article is çipem for both masculine and feminine plural nouns. (e.g., "çléidb çipem", the cats; "çqepçanéyp çipem", the houses.)

In summary, ipem is used with masculine singular nouns, éem with feminine singular nouns, and çipem with all plural nouns. This variation in definite articles reflects the grammatical gender and number of nouns in Idbqipèhj.

After é, ip, an, ep, af, x, èp, yv and some occurrences of id, the singular masculine article ipem becomes 'em.


-----
NOUNS
-----
* Gender
Every Idbqipèhj noun has a grammatical gender, either masculine or feminine.

* Number
As in English, Idbqipèhj nouns inflect for number, however they do so through prefixation rather than suffixation.

The plural is usually formed from the singular by adding the prefix morpheme à- (e.g., qepçanéyp > àqepçanéyp 'houses'). 

Nouns beginning with afé- and afip- take the prefix ç- instead of à- (e.g., aféxafl > àaféxafl 'pipes', afipèd > àafipèd 'games'), except for the nouns aféavqéem, aféèhèhéç, afipqc, and afipemw which form their plural by prefixing the morpheme ç- (e.g., afipqc > çafipqc 'tires').

Seven nouns beginning with afep- form their plural with à-. These are afepqipg, afepememanéb, afepwanid, afepèdanw, afepc, afepidb, and afepèdafepèd (e.g., afepqipg > àafepqipg 'knees'). All other nouns beginning with afep-, such as afepçanw or afepèhl, follow the regular plural pattern and take ç- (e.g., afepèhl > çafepèhl 'holes').

Nouns that begin with ç-, à- or z- in the singular do not change in the plural (e.g., àanepèhb éem 'the cross' > àanepèhb çipem 'the crosses').

Nouns that begin with emé- typically change to àafé- in the plural (e.g., eméqèhafepèd > àaféqèhafepèd 'newspapers'). However, several nouns beginning with emé- are exceptions to this rule and form their plural by adding ç- instead. These are eméw, eméb, eméyréqèhéb, emébéidb, eméyranlçipj, emélanbèpèh, eméyrèhipç and emégèpèh (e.g., eméyranlçipj ipem > çeméyranlçipj çipem).

Similarly, most nouns beginning with emané- change to àafé- in the plural. Examples of this pattern include emanéw, emanéèhepb, emanéypèp, emanéèhancafepç, emanéyréèhl, and emanéèhlanyr (e.g., emanéèhlanyr qaf > àaféèhlanyr çipav 'stained-glass windows'). However, some emané- nouns do not follow this pattern and form their plural with ç-, notably emanéèh, emanéèhanllé, emanéavqéidb, emanélèpav, emanéqèhipyrafepg and emanélèhepc (e.g., emanéèh ipem > çemanéèh çipem 'the rails').

* Case
Nouns in Idbqipèhj are not inflected for any other grammatical categories. (However, personal pronouns are inflected for case and person.)

----------
ADJECTIVES
----------

An adjective must agree in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Idbqipèhj adjectives therefore have four forms: masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural. A few adjectives, like aféipw and aféipyrafepq, have a fifth form, viz. an additional masculine singular form for use after a noun ending in é, ip, an, ep, af, x, èp, yv and some occurrences of id, e.g. qanavèhéèd aféipw qaf (a beautiful garden), ipypypepid emipw qaf (a handsome man), ipypypipj ipememipw ipqaf (a beautiful woman), çlqéjqip àaféipw çipem (the beautiful children), çqepçanéyp çipememipw çipem (the beautiful houses).

The masculine singular, an adjective's basic form, is listed in dictionaries. Most feminine forms are formed by adding the prefix ip- to the masculine form, e.g., avqéèhg > ipavqéèhg, lqipem > iplqipem, qéçèhipc > ipqéçèhipc. 

Under certain circumstances, other minor changes occur in the formation of feminine forms. Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with emip-, eman-, qep-, qip-, çep- or çé- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix ip- (e.g., emipafèhb > ipememipafèhb, emanlqipg > ipememanlqipg, qepw > ipqqepw, qipanbqé > ipqqipanbqé, çepèhg > ipççepèhg, and çéw > ipççéw).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with b- change to ipidb- (e.g., bqéemw > ipidbqéemw); those beginning with èhafip- or àafip- change to ipçafip- (e.g., èhafipllipypepèhc > ipçafipllipypepèhc, àafipanèhafj > ipçafipanèhafj), with the exception of the irregular àafipanyr (old) whose feminine form is ipememanipanyr; g- changes to ipafg- (e.g., gqepem > ipafgqepem); jan- changes to ipyran- (e.g., janlbé > ipyranlbé); jip- changes to ipyryv- (e.g., jipèhw > ipyryvèhw); èhip- changes to ipèhyv- (e.g., èhipgqéèhlèp > ipèhyvgqéèhlèp); lip- changes to iplyv- (e.g., lipanafkqan > iplyvanafkqan); and adjectives beginning with afep- have a special form emep- (becoming ipememep- in feminine) that appears after é, ip, an, ep, af, x, èp, yv and some occurrences of id, (e.g., afepj/emepj > ipememepj, afepyp/emepyp > ipememepyp).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with ip-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. ipidbanèh ipypypepid qaf 'a rich man' > ipidbanèh ipypypipj ipqaf 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix ç- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., anemepèd > çanemepèd, ipanemepèd > çipanemepèd). If the basic form beginning with ç-, à-, or z-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., çéw > çéw, àafipèhèpqèpg > àafipèhèpqèpg, àafepav > àafepav), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Idbqipèhj adjectives beginning with aféip- take the prefix à- in the masculine plural (e.g., aféipyrafepq > àaféipyrafepq). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with emé-, which normally change to àafé- in the masculine plural (e.g., eméqèhipyranid > àaféqèhipyranid, eméèhlqipb > àaféèhlqipb), with only two exceptions: eméléj > çeméléj and eméyréq > çeméyréq which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: ipeméèhlqipb > çipeméèhlqipb.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed before the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in ipgafepèh qanyr ipem (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically follow their nouns. These are aféipw (beautiful), qepw (good), jipèhw (brief), avqéèhg (big/tall), çepèhg (fat/large), àaféj (false), laféid (high), gqepem (long), jipèhw (brief), ipqafipèd (young), anemepèd (pretty), çanéyraféyp (bad), èhafipememanipyp (better), aféipyrafepq (new), lanlipc (small), àafipanyr (old); e.g., ipypypipj ipememipw ipqaf ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Idbqipèhj, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
idbqipèhj personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | ipèd
         | 2nd (informal)   | afl
         | 2nd (formal)     | çafepyr
         | 3rd (masculine)  | eman
         | 3rd (feminine)   | ipememip
         | 3rd (neutral)    | qep
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | çafepq
         | 2nd              | çafepyr
         | 3rd (masculine)  | çeman
         | 3rd (feminine)   | çipememip
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun ipèd occurs after é, ip, an, ep, af, x, èp, yv, ê and some occurrences of id, it becomes 'èd.

*Relative pronouns

idbqipèhj, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Idbqipèhj, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, anafk is ordinarily used: ipllipembxbanw éyp èpemepyr é anafk ipypypepid'em ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that anafk in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: çipèpemepyr èplèp lqep anafk çipllipembxbanw çipem ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, ipafk (or 'afk after é, ip, an, ep, af, x, èp, yv, ê and some occurrences of id) is ordinarily used: ipèpemepyr é eman'afk ipllipembxbanw éem ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like anafk, ipafk does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Idbqipèhj are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Idbqipèhj is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) èhanepyré ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of ipèhlê ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is ipèhlê, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is èhanepyré. Forms of ipèhlê are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Idbqipèhj, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

idbqipèhj verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -ççan- between the stem and the ending.

    In lqipanéemèhéc, the stem -emèhéc indicates that the verb is èhipemèhéc (to speak) and the prefix lqipané- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In çqepççanqanj, the stem -qanj indicates that the verb is èhanqanj (to finish), the prefix -ççan- precedes it, and the inflection çqep- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Idbqipèhj they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    èhipemèhéc: çanéèhipemèhéc ipèd, çéemèhéc afl, lqipççéemèhéc çeman'afk, çqepanemèhéc çafepq ipafk, zipemèhéc...
    èhanqanj: çanéèhanqanj ipèd, çiplîqanj çafepyr, lqipççanqanj çeman'afk, çanqanj, çqepanççanqanj çafepq ipafk...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    èhanepemafepyr: àafipyr ipèd, àafipyr afl, lafipyr eman, çqepemafepyr çafepq, zipemafepyr çafepyr, lqipemafipyr çeman.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly èhanepyré, ipèhlê, èhipememé and ipèhanéj), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with èhip- (with the exception of èhipememé, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    èhipypané, èhipxéeméw, èhiplqéidb, èhipxepyrqip, èhipypèhipj, èhipgqéyp, èhipççéc, èhipxéc, èhipqipypepèhc, èhipavèhégipèh, etc.

        For example, for the verb èhipemèhéc, the stem is -emèhéc and the infinitive prefix is èhip-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with èhan- whose present participle begins with lqéççan-:

    èhanqèpw, èhanlécypepb, èhancèhipafgèpav, èhanèhafipemj, èhanavqéèhg, èhïéid, èhanlçipyrqan, èhanemepc, èhangafepèh, èhangafèh, èhaneméç, etc.

        For example, for the verb èhanqanj, the stem is -qanj and the infinitive prefix is èhan-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries ipèhlê and èhanepyré, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. ipavèhégipèh ipèd means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with ipèh- (part of the third group): ç-, ç-, - , çqep-, zip-, lqip-.
