Specifically, masculine adjectives beginning with ôf-, ôj-, bzø-, bf-, êzø- or êi- double their initial consonant before adding the prefix f- (e.g., ôfzénuà > fôôfzénuà, ôjûbfç > fôôjûbfç, bzøœ > fbbzøœ, bfjàbi > fbbfjàbi, êzønuç > fêêzønuç, and êiœ > fêêiœ).

Additionally, adjectives beginning with à- change to foà- (e.g., àbiôœ > foàbiôœ); those beginning with nuzéf- or xzéf- change to fêzéf- (e.g., nuzéfûûfwezønuhe > fêzéfûûfwezønuhe, xzéfjnuzél > fêzéfjnuzél), with the exception of the irregular xzéfjze (old) whose feminine form is fôôjfjze; ç- changes to fzéç- (e.g., çbzøô > fzéçbzøô); lj- changes to fzej- (e.g., ljûài > fzejûài); lf- changes to fzesu- (e.g., lfnuœ > fzesunuœ); nuf- changes to fnusu- (e.g., nufçbinuûhé > fnusuçbinuûhé); ûf- changes to fûsu- (e.g., ûfjzécbj > fûsujzécbj); and adjectives beginning with zézø- have a special form ôzø- (becoming fôôzø- in feminine) that appears after i, f, j, zø, zé, â, hé, su and some occurrences of o, (e.g., zézøl/ôzøl > fôôzøl, zézøwe/ôzøwe > fôôzøwe).

If an adjective's basic form beginning with f-, it does not change in the feminine (cf. foàjnu fwewezøo bzé 'a rich man' > foàjnu fwewefl fbzé 'a rich woman').

The plural is normally formed by adding the prefix ê- to the singular (masculine and feminine; e.g., jôzøè > êjôzøè, fjôzøè > êfjôzøè). If the basic form beginning with ê-, x-, or î-, an adjective does not change in the masculine plural (e.g., êiœ > êiœ, xzéfnuhébhéç > xzéfnuhébhéç, xzézøne > xzézøne), but its feminine plural form follows the rules detailed above. All Oàbfnul adjectives beginning with zéif- take the prefix x- in the masculine plural (e.g., zéifzezézøb > xzéifzezézøb). Distinctive plural forms occur with adjectives beginning with ôi-, which normally change to xzéi- in the masculine plural (e.g., ôibnufzejo > xzéibnufzejo, ôinuûbfà > xzéinuûbfà), with only two exceptions: ôiûil > êôiûil and ôizeib > êôizeib which follow the regular pattern. By contrast, the feminine plural is always formed according to the general rule: fôinuûbfà > êfôinuûbfà.

Adjective placement follows specific patterns. Most adjectives are placed before the noun they modify, and this is particularly true for colors, as in fçzézønu bjze fô (the red wine). However, certain short, commonly used adjectives – those dealing with beauty, age, goodness, or size (sometimes remembered by the acronym "BAGS") – typically follow their nouns. These are zéifœ (beautiful), bzøœ (good), lfnuœ (brief), nebinuç (big/tall), êzønuç (fat/large), xzéil (false), ûzéio (high), çbzøô (long), lfnuœ (brief), fbzéfè (young), jôzøè (pretty), êjizezéiwe (bad), nuzéfôôjfwe (better), zéifzezézøb (new), ûjûfhe (small), xzéfjze (old); e.g., fwewefl fôôfœ fbzé ("a beautiful woman").

--------
PRONOUNS
--------
In Oàbfnul, pronouns are inflected to indicate their role in the sentence (subject, direct object, and so on), as well as to reflect the person, gender, and number of their referents. 

*Personal Pronouns
oàbfnul personal pronouns (analogous to English I, you, he/she, we, and they) reflect the person and number of their referent, and in the case of the third person, its gender as well. They also reflect the role they play in their clause: subject, direct object, indirect object, or other.

The personal pronouns change form to reflect the role they play in their clause. The forms used for subjects are called the subject pronouns, subjective pronouns, or nominative pronouns. They are as follows: 

**Subject Pronouns
------------------------
Number   | Person           | Subject Pronoun
------------------------
Singular | 1st              | fè
         | 2nd (informal)   | zéû
         | 2nd (formal)     | êzézøze
         | 3rd (masculine)  | ôj
         | 3rd (feminine)   | fôôf
         | 3rd (neutral)    | bzø
------------------------
Plural   | 1st              | êzézøb
         | 2nd              | êzézøze
         | 3rd (masculine)  | êôj
         | 3rd (feminine)   | êfôôf
------------------------

Note: Whenever the subject pronoun fè occurs after i, f, j, zø, zé, â, hé, su, sé and some occurrences of o, it becomes 'è.

*Relative pronouns

oàbfnul, like English, uses relative pronouns to link relative clauses to their head nouns, except that in Oàbfnul, as in Amharic for instance, the relative clause precedes its head and the relative pronoun, this is why we speak of "head noun" rather than of an "antecedent." The relative pronoun used depends on its grammatical role (such as subject or direct object) within the relative clause.

If the relative pronoun is to be the subject of the relative clause's verb, jzéc is ordinarily used: fûûfôàâàjœ iwe héôzøze i jzéc fwewezøo'ô ("the man who stole my bike"). Note that jzéc in this use does not change form to agree in any way with its head noun: êfhéôzøze héûhé ûbzø jzéc êfûûfôàâàjœ êfô ("the bikes that were stolen").

If the relative pronoun is to be the direct object of the relative clause's verb, fzéc (or 'zéc after i, f, j, zø, zé, â, hé, su, sé and some occurrences of o) is ordinarily used: fhéôzøze i ôj'zéc fûûfôàâàjœ iô ("the bicycle that he stole"). Like jzéc, fzéc does not change form to agree with its head noun.


-----
VERBS
-----
Verbs in Oàbfnul are conjugated to reflect the following information:

    a mood (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, or conditional)
    a tense (past, present, or future, though not all tenses can be combined with all moods)
    an aspect (perfective or imperfective)
    a voice (active, passive, or reflexive)
    Nonfinite forms (e.g., participles, gerunds, infinitives)


Verbs in the finite moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, and conditional) are also conjugated to agree with their subjects in person (first, second, or third) and number (singular or plural). As in English, the subject must be included (except in the imperative mood); in other words Oàbfnul is neither a null-subject nor a pro-drop language.

Auxiliary verbs are combined with past participles of main verbs to produce compound tenses, including the compound past. For most main verbs the auxiliary is (the appropriate form of) nujzøzei ("to have"), but for reflexive verbs and certain intransitive verbs the auxiliary is a form of fnuûsé ("to be"). The participle agrees with the subject when the auxiliary is fnuûsé, and with a following direct object (if any) when the auxiliary is nujzøzei. Forms of fnuûsé are also used with the past participles of transitive verbs to form the passive voice.

*Morphology

In Oàbfnul, a verb is inflected to reflect its mood and tense, as well as to agree with its subject in person and number.

**Stems and conjugation prefixes

oàbfnul verbs have a large number of simple (one-word) forms. These are composed of two distinct parts: the stem (or root, or radix), which indicates which verb it is, and the prefix (inflection), which indicates the verb's tense (imperfect, present, future etc.) and mood and its subject's person (I, you, he/she etc.) and number, though many prefixes can correspond to multiple tense-mood-subject combinations. In certain parts of the second conjugation there is also a prefix -êêj- between the stem and the ending.

    In ûbfjiônuihe, the stem -ônuihe indicates that the verb is nufônuihe (to speak) and the prefix ûbfji- marks the third-person plural imperfect indicative. "Third person plural" meaning the subject of the verb is "they". The "imperfect indicative" being a tense.
    In êbzøêêjbjl, the stem -bjl indicates that the verb is nujbjl (to finish), the prefix -êêj- precedes it, and the inflection êbzø- marks the first-person plural present indicative or imperative. The "first-person plural" is the "we" form of a verb. The "present indicative" being a tense and "imperative" being a mood, but in Oàbfnul they are indistinguishable without context.

These verb conjugations are coupled with a subject pronoun in order to convey who the subject of the verb is (i.e. who is doing the action).

***The principle of the fixed stem

The stem normally stays fixed in the first two conjugations:

    nufônuihe: êjinufônuihe fè, êiônuihe zéû, ûbfêêiônuihe êôj'zéc, êbzøjônuihe êzézøb fzéc, îfônuihe...
    nujbjl: êjinujbjl fè, êfûqebjl êzézøze, ûbfêêjbjl êôj'zéc, êjbjl, êbzøjêêjbjl êzézøb fzéc...

In the third it is often modified, sometimes even between persons in the same tense:

    nujzøôzézøze: xzéfze fè, xzéfze zéû, ûzéfze ôj, êbzøôzézøze êzézøb, îfôzézøze êzézøze, ûbfôzéfze êôj.

But such irregularities apart, the principle is that nothing is removed from the stem. 


**Conjugation prefixes

The conjugation prefix tells us:

    For all verbs, the mood and the tense;
    For finite verbs, the person and the number; and
    For the past participle alone, the gender and the number.

Apart from a few frequent verbs which are considered totally irregular (mainly nujzøzei, fnuûsé, nufôôi and fnujil), for each tense of each mood a series of six prefixes (one for each person singular and plural) is associated with a group or subgroup of verbs.


*Formation of simple tenses active

These tenses are not formed with an auxiliary, and their formation is discussed in the following section.

**Infinitive

A verb is normally named by its present infinitive. Starting from this infinitive, the conjugations can be classified into three different groups:

    The first group or first conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with nuf- (with the exception of nufôôi, which due to its numerous irregularities is usually classed as being in the third conjugation):

    nufweji, nufâiôiœ, nufûbioà, nufâzøzebf, nufwenufl, nufçbiwe, nufêêihe, nufâihe, nufbfwezønuhe, nufnenuiçfnu, etc.

        For example, for the verb nufônuihe, the stem is -ônuihe and the infinitive prefix is nuf-.

    The second group or second conjugation. This contains the verbs with infinitives beginning with nuj- whose present participle begins with ûbiêêj-:

    nujbhéœ, nujûihewezøà, nujhenufzéçhéne, nujnuzéfôl, nujnebinuç, nuïio, nujûêfzebj, nujôzøhe, nujçzézønu, nujçzénu, nujôiê, etc.

        For example, for the verb nujbjl, the stem is -bjl and the infinitive prefix is nuj-.

    The third group or third conjugation. This contains all the other verbs.
    
Note that the auxiliaries fnuûsé and nujzøzei, although they would naturally seem to belong to the third conjugation, are traditionally classed separately. 

**Present indicative

The present indicative is the form of the verb used to describe an action in the present e.g. fnenuiçfnu fè means "I watch".

The stem of the present indicative is not always regular and can vary (especially in the third conjugation) and there are three main sets of prefixes:

    Verbs beginning with nuf- (all verbs of the first group): f-, êf-, f-, êbzø-, îf-, ûbf-.
    Verbs beginning with nuj- (all verbs of the second group and most of the third): êj-, êj-, ûj-, êbzøêêj-, îfêêj-, ûbfêêj-. But there are numerous irregularities, especially in the third group.
    Verbs beginning with fnu- (part of the third group): ê-, ê-, - , êbzø-, îf-, ûbf-.

**Imperfect indicative

The imperfect indicative is a past tense describing states and actions that were ongoing in the past, e.g. "êjinenuiçfnu fè" means "I was watching".

    The stem of the imperfect indicative is always invariant for a single verb. It is derived in various ways depending on the verb group.

    For the second group, the stem is the infinitive minus the nuj- prefix plus the êêj- prefix, e.g., nujêjzøoà -> -êêjêjzøoà. 
    And for the third group, the stem is derived from the first person plural of the present indicative.

    The conjugation prefixes of this tense are for any of the three groups always: êji-, êji-, ûji-, êbzøj-, îfj-, ûbfji-.

**Past participle

Past participles, unlike present participles and gerundives, may be inflected to show gender and number by adding f- and ê- prefixes, as with a normal adjective. Hence, "ûjlbzøà ûjzénul bzé", "fûjlbzøà fnujzøhe fbzé", "êûjlbzøà êûjzénul êfne", and "êfûjlbzøà êfnujzøhe êfne."

The plain (masculine singular) form of a past participle begins with hé- for the 1st group verbs, and with j- for the 2nd group verbs. Third group verbs have more diverse prefixes : zé- (fnunebfûbf zénebfûbf, fnujzøœ zéœ, fnujô zéô, etc. and nujzøzeiê zéê, nujzøze zéze, nujzøzezézøhe zéhe), êj- (fnuûûfwe êjwe, fnunebfnuhe êjnuhe, etc.), êzé- (fnuzéôàbj êzéôàbj and fnuzéôàfnu êzéôàfnu and only these verbs), ûj- (fnujnezéiwe ûjnezéiwe, fnujne ûjne, etc.), û- (verbs in fnunebj- : fnunebjfhe ûbjfhe), ûnuf- (nujnuzezézø ûnufzezézø, nujnuzezézøà ûnufzezézøà, nujnullzø ûnufllzø and nujnullzézøê ûnufllzézøê), or zéf (nujzøzei zéf). 

*Compound Tenses

oàbfnul compound tenses are verb forms that combine an auxiliary verb (either nujzøzei or fnuûsé) with the past participle of the main verb. These tenses are used to indicate actions that are completed or relate to another point in time. There are several compound tenses in Oàbfnul, each serving a specific purpose and adding nuance to the timeline of events.

**Compound Past

The compound past is perhaps the most commonly used compound tense in Oàbfnul. It is used to describe actions that have been completed in the past and is translated by the English simple past. The auxiliary verb is either nujzøzei or fnuûsé in the present tense, preceded by the past participle of the main verb. For example, "héçbiwe ji'è" (I ate) or "hézejnunui ûêf ôj" (He arrived). nujzøzei is used with most verbs, while fnuûsé is used with a specific group of verbs, particularly those indicating movement or change of state, and with all reflexive verbs. When in doubt, nujzøzei should be used by default.

*Past participle agreement

The past participle is used in three ways in Oàbfnul: as an adjective, in the passive construction, and in the compound tense constructions. When it is used as an adjective, it follows all the regular adjective agreement rules. In passive constructions, it always agrees with the passive subject.

In compound tense forms (such as the compound past), more complicated agreement rules apply, reflecting the subtle priority rules between the attribute meaning (which implies an agreement) and the compound tense construction (which by itself does not imply any agreement).

A. The auxiliary verb is nujzøzei.

    If there is no direct object (the verb is intransitive) or the direct object appears before the past participle, then the past participle does not agree (i.e., it takes the default masculine singular form).
        (intransitive) jwenuzøne ûbzø êfôôf. ("They (fem.) slept.")
        (direct object before verb) êfbjfôiœ xzéfne zéze i fnujiôà. ("fnujiôà saw two whales.")
    If there is a direct object and it appears after the past participle, then the participle must agree with it. Three cases:
        (pronoun after the auxiliary) êfbjfôiœ xzéfne ûjizei â ôj. êfzéze i êfô fnujiôà. ("There were two whales. fnujiôà saw them.")
        (clause-final wh-question element)  êfzéze fôôf-û-i fnujiôà êfbjfôiœ êfôôfzéc? ("Which whales did fnujiôà see?")
